en: *The Miscellaneous Collection of Dhāraṇīs*, Scroll One.
The author is unknown; it is currently appended to the Liang dynasty catalog.
It contains fifteen dhāraṇī spells in total, comprising the great dhāraṇī divine spells spoken by the Seven Buddhas and the divine spells spoken by eight bodhisattvas.
The Buddha Vipaśyin taught that there are eighteen thousand illnesses,
all of which are completely cured by a single incantation.
This dhāraṇī is named Suluduhaka.
In the Jin language, this is the definitive Sanskrit sound:

*Cīpācīpā*, *hūnupācīpā hūnupācīpā*, *ajñapācīpā ajñapācīpā*, *dohunapācīpā*, *śamanupācīpā*, *huṣuditanapācīpā*, *mijihunapācīpā*, *ihuditānapācīpā*, *milijidititanapācīpā*, *sajñadititanapācīpā*, *mijñanuditānapācīpā*, *ucchaduditānapācīpā*. *Svāhā*. Recite this mantra three times.
Tie fourteen knots with yellow thread;
bind one knot around the neck for each phrase of the mantra.
By the power of this dhāraṇī, all [obstacles] can be utterly subdued.
They can move mountains, cut off flowing rivers, dry up the great oceans, and crush all mountains into fine dust like motes.
If the sun and moon lose their proper courses, they can cause them to proceed correctly and entirely dispel all calamities.
It can cause wind and rain to fall out of season, yet it can also regulate the proper seasons;
it can cause grain crops to fail, yet it can also bring about abundant harvests;
and when neighboring states invade its borders, it can entirely repel them.
The evil intent of ministers who plot rebellion is immediately extinguished.
Pestilence and calamities that arise can all be warded off.
When pestilential demons enter the country, they can be driven away.
When the kalpa of weapons arises, it can destroy and extinguish them.
The power of this dhāraṇī wards off calamities and eliminates anomalies in measureless and boundless ways;
were one to explain it in detail, it would not be exhausted even at the end of an eon.
The second formula is the dhāraṇī spoken by the Buddha named Husuduō;
in the Jin language, it means "removing all oppressive heat and afflictions.
These are the words of this dhāraṇī.
The divine incantations spoken by seventy-two billion Buddhas:

*tama-dina*, *cāpauttina*, *śaphu-śaphutina*, *usudu-usudutina*, *phuphuśa-phuphuśatina*, *aśuti-aśutitina*, *nirica-niricatina*, *cipahā-cipahūtina*, *suhadu-suhadutina*, *yamuśa-yamuśatina*, *śapabudina*, *augibudina*, *susabudina*. *Svāhā*. Recite this incantation three times.
Tie three knots with yellow thread and fasten them around the neck.
By the spiritual power of this dhāraṇī,
it can cause the trichiliocosm to shake in six ways.
Mountains, rivers, rocks, and cliffs will tremble, leap, and submerge;
all sentient beings therein shall give rise to the unsurpassed mind of bodhi,
thereby able to eliminate the heavy sins of birth and death accumulated over seventy-seven billion kalpas.
All sufferings of illness shall be completely extinguished without remainder.
Among those sentient beings who write down, read, or recite even a single phrase of this dhāraṇī, [all their ailments shall likewise be eliminated].
In worlds as numerous as the sands of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Ganges Rivers,
heavy and evil karmic offenses shall be crushed and extinguished without remainder.
The third divine mantra spoken by the Buddha Anupamarāja is named Mṛgīdatta.
The Jin language calls it the "Golden Drum.
It is capable of utterly destroying, without remainder, all the karmic obstructions, retributive obstructions, heavy defilements, and afflictions possessed by sentient beings.

Pulude nā, yamudhine nā, aṅgudhine nā, yamudhine nā, chabubhine nā, yamudhine nā, usahuhuhine nā, yamudhine nā, śampabhūbhuhine nā, kaurīṭabhūbhuhine nā, chapaduhine nā, yajñanahine nā, ushabhuhine nā, chatūrīnahine nā. Svāhā. Recite this mantra seven times.
Tie four knots with yellow thread around the neck;
these dhāraṇī phrases were spoken by as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.
For anyone who writes down or recites this dhāraṇī,
all their heavy evils, karmic obstacles, and obstacles to retribution from kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges shall be [eliminated].
Furthermore, the five heinous crimes and the offenses of the icchantikas shall all be extinguished without remainder.
All the grave illnesses and obstacles to the Path possessed by sentient beings [shall likewise be eliminated].
The stains of transgression and the stains of karma—
all these will be extinguished without remainder upon hearing what he says.
Furthermore, for those who copy, read, or recite it:
In whatever places they may go— whether kingdoms, cities, villages, mountain forests, or burial mounds—
if sentient beings there hear the name of this dhāraṇī being recited,
even if it enters their ears but once, after their lives have ended, [they shall attain liberation].
All shall attain rebirth in the land of Akṣobhya Buddha;
until they achieve Buddhahood, they shall not fall into the three miserable realms.
By practicing this dhāraṇī method, [this result is attained].
On the sixteenth day of the fourth month, within the east-facing stūpa,
he circumambulated the stūpa eighty times in a single day.
He then stood facing east beneath the western wall of the stūpa.
Recite the mantra twenty-four times.
Do not sleep for seven days and seven nights.
You must prepare seven lamps using sesame oil or hempseed oil.
Place it at the four corners of the stupa.
Bathe thoroughly and cleanly, put on new, pure garments,
and abstain from alcohol, meat, and the five pungent roots.
When they encounter their midday meal,
I shall appear before that person at that time,
emitting great radiance with my golden hand.
He stroked the crown of his head and immediately conferred upon him the prediction of enlightenment.
All the karmic obstructions and defilements of this person were extinguished without remainder.
The fourth Buddha, Krakucchanda, was about to preach a great dhāraṇī named Vajradhvaja.
And it can cure the sentient beings of the three realms who are afflicted by the five turbidities,
as well as the grave illnesses of all evil afflictions,
karmic obstructions, and retributive obstructions.
It can completely eliminate all defilements and afflictions.
*Dhyānadhūṭa*; in the Jin language, this means "to extract sentient beings from suffering and cause them to emerge from the mire of desire."
Those who hear it are liberated from the three defilements: greed, hatred, and pride.
This is the *Ajñāpaya-vijñāpayati*.
Nahetu gīvo ajjodī nahetu sakhupamo hetu.
If there were no akṣi-dyūṣa-kṣama-akṣi-gīva-makṣi.
Cchā-tu-ri-na-he-dyu-phu-ri-te-na-he-dyu-a-hu-hu-ya-he-dyu.
Pulite he zhòu zhānán móulidì (in the Jin language:
"Great Abundance and Fulness") qífú mó móxiū.
Bhata mumuḥumuri nu buhuḥu śrayatu buhuḥu cī-aprabha buhuḥu.
Aṅgīrasa pū pū pū khyu buri-te yi pū pū khyu svāhā.
Recite this mantra once; take yellow thread, tie thirteen knots, and fasten it around the neck.
All the dharani phrases mentioned above, as well as those spoken by me,
have been spoken by ninety-nine billion Buddhas of the past.
Should there be anyone who reads, recites, or transcribes them, [they shall obtain great merit].
In this very life, one shall attain the Vajradhvaja Samādhi.
All fetters and afflictions will be utterly destroyed without remainder.
One shall rescue and deliver sentient beings from suffering as described above.
His spiritual powers were sovereign and immeasurable.
The fifth Buddha, Kanakamuni,
desired to proclaim the great dhāraṇī named Vidyutjihva.
The sound of his speech resounds throughout the ten directions, such that none do not submit;
he awakens sentient beings like the roll of thunder,
causing those in ignorance to obtain the eye of wisdom.
These dharani phrases were spoken by seventy-two billion buddhas of the past;
I now proclaim them.

Cana-pāratīṇaṃ, anaṇagihanaṃ, usagihanaṃ, dhavugihanaṃ, pulitigihanaṃ, kṣayanaṃgihanaṃ, kimpāratīṇaṃgihanaṃ, mitigatīṇaṃgihanaṃ, aranyagatīṇaṃvihanaṃ, hupadatīṇaṃgilanaṃ, mitigadutīṇaṃjyomahatīṇaṃ, u-u-u-uhadatīṇaṃ, jipravatīṇaṃ, svāhā. Recite this mantra three times. Tie yellow thread into three knots and bind them to the site of pain.
By the power of this dhāraṇī,
it can cause the trichiliocosm to shake in six ways, and all sentient beings therein—
If one hears the exposition of these dharani phrases even once,
it shall last for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of koṭis of kalpas.
All grave offenses, including the five heinous crimes of slander, shall be extinguished without remainder.
If there are sentient beings who practice this by reciting it for seven days and seven nights, reducing their sleep, [their transgressions will likewise be purified].
That person, in their present body, attains the Lion King Samādhi.
Hundreds of thousands of Buddhas appear before them and bestow predictions of enlightenment.
Furthermore, if powerful enemies from neighboring lands should come to invade and harass that country, [they shall be subdued].
At that time, the king, together with his various ministers,
bathed himself thoroughly in purity, donned fresh clean garments,
and stood upon a high terrace facing the respective directions.
First, pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions;
then, pay homage to me, Krakucchanda-Muni Buddha.
Recite my name three times, burn incense, and scatter flowers.
At that time, he immediately spoke these dharani phrases.
By the majestic spiritual power of this dharani,
Mahābrahmā, Śakra, and the Four Great Heavenly Kings—
From the midst of the void, swords and blades rained down everywhere;
great black winds arose from the four quarters,
causing all the soldiers to be unable to see the light of the sun or moon.
The hosts of yakṣas will suck away their vital essence;
those who were destined to die will die, and others will naturally retreat and disperse.
Such is the power of the majesty of this great dhāraṇī.
The sixth was Kāśyapa Buddha.
He wished to preach the Great Dhāraṇī named *Cūḍāmaṇi*,
which in the Jin language means "Rescuing and Delivering All Sentient Beings from the Suffering of Birth and Death."

Ajñāta-devilinda, Cāmara-devilinda, Uśanā-devilinda, Śakrapārājitā-devilinda, Vāsava-pārājitā-devilinda, Nahuṣa-pārājitā-devilinda, Nāciketa-pārājitā-devilinda, Nahutara-devilinda, Vāyu-pratara-devilinda, Nabhodura-devilinda, Śyāma-durādevilinda. Svāhā. Recite this mantra seven times.
Tie six knots with yellow thread and bind them to the site of pain.
This is the dharani phrase.
This is that which was spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas of the past.
By the power of this dhāraṇī,
it can cause the hundred Buddha-worlds to quake in six ways.
All mountains, rivers, rocks,
and cliffs were completely shattered like fine dust,
becoming entirely one Buddha-world.
Within it, all things whatsoever became golden in color;
the vast expanse and shimmering depths no longer appeared,
and one saw only gold with no other colors remaining.
By the power of this dhāraṇī,
it is able to cause the sentient beings of a hundred buddha-worlds to eliminate the heavy karmic offenses of their past lives as well as the sufferings of the three miserable realms.
All shall be completely extinguished without remainder.
Among those sentient beings who practice and recite this dhāraṇī,
there are some who have not yet resolved to attain unsurpassed bodhicitta.
May all cause their minds to be awakened and reach the stage of non-retrogression.
As for those who have already awakened their minds,
they should practice this dhāraṇī.
Surpassing the seventh stage up to the tenth stage—
this is the Vajra-samādhi Great Emptiness Liberation Gate of this dhāraṇī.
From the first generation of the mind of awakening, the bodhisattva practices this samādhi.
Even until he reached the site of enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree and entered the Vajra-samādhi,
it was all not without this [cause].
This is the seventh Śākyamuni Buddha.
I shall now proclaim the name of the Great Dhāraṇī called *Uṣṇīṣavijayā*.
In the Jin language, it means "Golden Light Radiance.
It dispels the darkness and obscurations of sentient beings within the three realms and delivers them from their calamities and hardships.
This dhāraṇī phrase was spoken by ninety-nine billion Buddhas of the past;
I now proclaim it:

Kilubudinaḍi | Bhiḍinaḍi | Usudinaḍi | Gumudinaḍi | Yajudinaḍi | Ajñāśayadinaḍi | Jayadinaḍi | Gumuprajādinaḍi | Ugipudinaḍi | Migisudinaḍi | Yamigidinaḍi | Prājimidinaḍi | Bhiliḍitādinaḍi | Svāhā. Recite this mantra fourteen times.
Tie fourteen knots with yellow thread and bind them to the site of pain;
by the power of this dhāraṇī, [it shall be healed].
It can cause the trichiliocosm to shake in six ways; therein,
the sentient beings who have been entangled, bound,
and fettered by the karmic stains of their past lives, remaining in dark and hidden places.
Upon hearing this dhāraṇī even once, its single sound reaching their ears,
all shall attain rebirth in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
There are those practitioners who...
Those who uphold, recite, read, and transcribe this dhāraṇī shall cause all who have not yet resolved their minds to resolve them and reach the stage of firmness;
those who have already resolved their minds shall enter the stream of the Dharma.
Abiding in the eighth stage, they will swiftly reach the ground of Buddhahood.
By the power of this dhāraṇī,
they shall leap over it all in a single bound beneath the Bodhi tree.
Even unto the stage of Buddhahood, sitting at the site of enlightenment—
this samādhi is named the King of Golden Light Samādhi;
it awakens all sentient beings, causes them to leap forth from the three realms, and uproots all their calamities and hardships.
One shall transcend the multitude of sages and swiftly attain the path of Buddhahood.
If there are sentient beings who wish to practice this dhāraṇī and desire to obtain the four fruits of the śramaṇa in their present body, [they shall succeed].
One wishes to eliminate the obstacles to the Path and the five heinous crimes committed over hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas in the past;
may these be extinguished in the present life so that not a single trace remains.
One should practice this dhāraṇī for twenty-one days— three times seven days—
upholding the prohibitive precepts as carefully as one would a bright pearl.
For one day and one night, practice the Way and repent toward the ten directions during the six periods;
bathe thoroughly and cleanly, don new and pure robes,
and use flowers of seven colors and three kinds of renowned incense.
One should make offerings and pay homage to Śākyamuni Buddha;
before the stūpa of his relics, one should prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground to repent and reform.
At that time, one should recite these dhāraṇī phrases eighty times.
He did so every day for up to seven days; yet,
even after one week, he had not obtained it.
Furthermore, after seven days, and even up to twenty-one days,
all heavy sins committed throughout hundreds of billions of kalpas will be extinguished without remainder.
The Buddhas of the ten directions will emit great rays of light that touch their bodies, and at that time, this person’s mind and heart will be filled with joy and serenity.
It is just as when a bhikṣu attains the third dhyāna;
at that time, Mahābrahmā, Śakra Devendra, and the Four Great Kings immediately bestow upon him the four fruits of śrāmaṇya.
The dharani spoken by Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva is named Yamadū;
in the Jin language, it means "Releasing the Bonds of Sentient Beings.
All present sufferings of illness are completely eliminated through it.
It can repel obstacles to the Path and extract the arrows of the three poisons;
the ninety-eight latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) are gradually extinguished;
one crosses the current of the three realms of existence (*trai-dhātuka*) and attains the Way in this very body.

Cīpudantī | Jambūcīdantī | Sucubhucīdantī | Cukibhucīdantī Usudacīdantī | Sacabhu-cīdantī | Yamalāyaṇicīdantī | Asupālāyaṇicīdantī | Supatidantī | Svāhā. Recite this mantra three times, tie five-colored thread into two knots, and fasten it around the neck.
This dhāraṇī was spoken by forty-two billion Buddhas.
If there are practitioners who are able to copy, read, or recite this dhāraṇī, they shall be protected in the present life by a thousand Buddhas;
when such a person’s life ends, they shall not fall into the evil realms.
One shall be born in the Tuṣita Heaven above to behold Maitreya face-to-face.
Furthermore, there are sentient beings who are able to practice this dhāraṇī;
they should fast for seven days and consume only cow’s milk.
One should eat only one meal at midday and not consume any other food.
Day and night, during the six periods,
one should repent before the Buddhas of the ten directions for all past misdeeds committed.
All heavy offenses committed throughout billions of kalpas will be completely extinguished at once;
even those who have violated the precepts in various ways will likewise be entirely purified.
This includes the calamities and evils of the five heinous crimes as well as the icchantikas.
By repenting with deep sincerity, all [faults] shall be completely extinguished.
During the six periods of the day, recite ten times during each period,
whether in a secluded, pure room or within a stūpa.
If this person’s mind is pure and sincere,
I shall go to their place at that time;
because they see me, their mind will become even more pure and sincere.
Because their minds are pure and profound, they are able to see a thousand Buddhas.
The Buddhas stroke their heads with their hands and immediately bestow upon them the prediction of enlightenment (vyākaraṇa).
The calamities and evils of their past lives are forever extinguished without remainder.
I, the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, wish to proclaim a great dhāraṇī named Anaji-zhou-ning.
In the Jin language, it is called "Extracting the Suffering of Sentient Beings"; it stands preeminent within the three realms, peerless and incomparable.
If there are sentient beings wandering through the six realms of rebirth who cannot be saved by others, I shall save them and cause them to escape their hardships.
Anaji zhousu, Buli diji zhousu, Ruopo zhousu, Pilidi naji zhousu, Ruyu bianshi ji zhousu, Wushadi nashe zhousu, Ruopo zhousu, Aruohupu ji zhousu. Svāhā. Recite this mantra five times.
Tie fourteen knots with a thread of five colors and fasten them to both hands.
This dhāraṇī was spoken by seventy-two billion Buddhas of the past;
I have now spoken it as well.
It is for the sake of protecting the True Dharma, for the sake of delivering sentient beings,
for the sake of perfecting the virtues of all practitioners through the ten thousand practices,
and for the sake of causing those among the śrāvakas who have not yet realized the fruit to attain it.
It causes those who are pratyekabuddhas to cross the great river of the twelve links of dependent origination and rescue all sentient beings;
it causes all bodhisattvas, from their first aspiration until the tenth stage, to fulfill the fruits of their vows.
He spoke this dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, by the power of this dhāraṇī,
it is able to cause the trichiliocosm—
Among those sentient beings dwelling in dark and hidden places or within the three miserable realms,
should this dhāraṇī reach their ears even once, they will attain the knowledge of past lives; furthermore,
they shall all achieve liberation from up to fourteen lifetimes.
If there are good men or good women who wish to practice this dhāraṇī,
they should do so for twenty-one days— three times seven.
Having purified oneself by bathing and donned new,
clean garments, one should go to a temple or a pure location during the final watch of the night when the morning star has risen.
Speak this at the time of the Great Star;
speak it for me to the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
Thus he spoke three times.
"May my root offenses be removed.
Thus he says three times.
"May my offenses that obstruct the Path be removed."
Thus he spoke three times:
"Grant me the four fruits of the śramaṇa.
Thus he spoke three times.
At that time, I immediately went to his place;
standing before that person, I received from him the four fruits of śrāmaṇya.
I vowed, "I shall grant them," and so it was said three times.
Burn aloeswood incense.
If, in a dream, one obtains an āmalaka fruit,
or a harītakī fruit, or a bimba fruit, or a vibhītaka fruit, or apricots and the like.
At that time, one should apply oneself with diligent effort;
whether it be like a hen’s egg or like a rolled-up scroll,
at that moment the morning star will appear.
At that time, recite the mantra seven times;
if the mind is favorable, recite it seventy times.
The Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha constantly travels through various lands.
For the sake of all practitioners so that they may proceed from the ten thousand practices—
this is what it means to proceed from the ten thousand practices—
I, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, wish to proclaim the Great Dhāraṇī.
Named Anaji, who does not know the limit of knowledge.
In the Jin language, this means "Great Realization that Universally Benefits Boundless Beings of the Ten Directions.

Oṣadhināga, Jñānāgajñāna, Akatunadeva, Naśupulideva, Amāśupulideva, Oṣahuḍhadeva, Ghibhūbhudeva, Kṣudhudeva, Jayabhūmanaradeva, Aukunaradeva, Cīpabunaradeva, Jambubharadeva. Svāhā. Recite this mantra five times.
Tie twenty-four knots with threads of five colors around the neck;
these dhāraṇī phrases were spoken by nine billion nine hundred million Buddhas of the past.
Ninety-nine billion Buddhas [bestow this upon] those practitioners who cultivate the six perfections but have not yet resolved their minds for enlightenment,
as well as those śrāvakas who have not yet realized the fruits of the path.
If there are any sages and seers within this trichiliocosm who have not yet resolved to attain unsurpassed bodhicitta,
may they all be inspired to do so.
There are ordinary beings who have not yet attained faith;
by means of these seeds, I cause the sprouts of the Dharma to grow through the majestic spiritual power of this dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, by means of my skillful means and majestic spiritual power,
may all that they cultivate be fully accomplished,
as well as within this trichiliocosm.
Sentient beings who are in secluded obscurity, darkness, or stagnation, as well as those in the three miserable realms—
all shall be liberated from suffering upon hearing this *dhāraṇī* of mine.
Furthermore, those bodhisattvas who have not yet reached the first stage shall attain the first stage.
They are led step by step until they attain the tenth stage (*bhūmi*).
Those who have already attained the first ten stages do so because of the power of this *dhāraṇī*.
In a single moment of thought, one will reach the stage of Buddhahood,
spontaneously accomplishing the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor characteristics.
If a śrāvaka hears this dhāraṇī even once, it passing through their ears, [the same result shall follow].
By reading, reciting, copying, and practicing this dhāraṇī,
and by abiding in accordance with the Dharma with a straightforward mind,
one will attain the four fruits of śrāmaṇya without seeking them.
By the power of this dhāraṇī, the mountains,
rivers, stone walls, and the waters of the four great oceans within the trichiliocosm can be made to surge and boil.
Mount Sumeru and the Iron Ring Mountains were reduced to the size of fine dust.
Among the sentient beings therein, there were bodhisattvas and śrāvakas engaged in spiritual practice who were hindered by obstacles to the Path and afflicted by impediments and suffering.
I shall rescue them all and cause them to be delivered from their perils.
I shall cause whatever they cultivate to be fully accomplished.
If there are sentient beings who seek their aspirations in the present life, [I shall grant them].
One who practices this dhāraṇī should maintain pure observance of the precepts for twenty-one days— three periods of seven days—
and perform the path of practice during the six periods of each day and night.
They burned various famous incenses and scattered five-colored flowers.
They repented of their own transgressions throughout the ten directions,
from the limits of birth and death to the limits of birth and death.
Feeling deep shame and remorse,
they then invoked the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva three times,
burning incense, scattering flowers, prostrating themselves, and seeking compassion while repenting for their transgressions and feeling ashamed.
All heavy sins accumulated over hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas will be completely extinguished in a single moment of thought,
purifying one’s body, speech, and mind.
At that time, one should recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times—
three times seven— six times each day,
from the first day until the seventh day.
Up until the twenty-first day,
those of dull faculties who have not yet attained the first fruit [of the path].
At that time, I bestow upon them the first fruit, the second, the third, and even the fourth fruit,
according to their respective capacities and the gradations of their faculties, whether sharp or dull.
If there are bodhisattvas who wish to progress toward the realization of the stages but are hindered and fail to advance, [I provide them with the necessary means].
One who practices according to the Dharma shall immediately attain the realization of the stages.
As previously taught, I now declare this dhāraṇī phrase.
Within this trichiliocosm,
there are all the Buddhas, the great Bodhisattvas,
Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Heavenly Kings, various ṛṣis, and the dragon kings.
All have fully realized and known that their great vows are accomplished;
may the fruits of these vows not be in vain, but be truly and exactly as such.
I, the Bodhisattva Jiejiu tuo (Sarvatrāṇa), now wish to proclaim a great dhāraṇī.
He is named Anagijira;
in the Jin language, this means "Rescuer from the Suffering of All Diseases" and "Destroyer of All Poisonous Medicines.
He delivers all sentient beings, causing them to emerge from birth and death.
Those who have not yet crossed over shall be crossed over; those who have not yet attained peace shall be brought to peace;
those who have not yet attained nirvana shall be made to attain nirvana.
This is the dharani phrase.
This was indeed spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas of the past.
I now wish to recite it:
*dhamarati anavarati kucinaṭi kimanati kuṭavaratataṭi asphālanati brahmaparinā-uśakini paṭarasati usunavarati dhamarati svāhā*. Recite this mantra three times.
Tie a cord of five colors into six knots and fasten them to both shoulders.
As I now recite these words of the dhāraṇī,
throughout the trichiliocosm...
All the karmic defilements, calamities, evils, and grave illnesses of all sentient beings therein—
by means of the resonance of my Dharma-voice shaking the trichiliocosm—
are dispersed and enter the pores of all sentient beings.
The feverish, toxic vapors of the present afflictions of the six sense-faculties and the burning distress of the various fetters of past karma are all completely extinguished,
leaving nothing behind.
Furthermore, there are practitioners who feel weary of and detached from the three realms;
though they desire to seek the definitive escape, they are unable to attain it.
I shall establish immeasurable skillful means for them.
May their respective aspirations be fulfilled.
Should there be neighboring enemies in that land who wish to invade and oppress,

If any kings, at the end of the final millennium of Śākyamuni Buddha’s teaching,
wish to seek the fulfillment of their aspirations, [they shall succeed].
It should also be thus;
there is no difference from the kings and others of old.
I, the Nāga King Utpalaka, now wish to proclaim a divine mantra.
His name is Itigoumo;
in the Jin language, it means "one who accords with the minds of sentient beings and does not oppose their intentions.
He is like the great ocean, fully endowed with the seven treasures.
Those who take [it] shall all obtain it;
those who do not take it are not at fault due to the Dragon King.
*Udu hulu du, jipadu, sukha du, jimadu, uṭṭa du, yamijidu, piliḍinadu, usudu, svāhā.* Recite this mantra three times; tie red and white threads into eight knots and fasten them around the neck.
This great divine mantra was spoken by twenty Ganges-sands of Buddhas in the past.
I have received this dhāraṇī from those Buddhas.
From that time until now, throughout a hundred *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas,
he has possessed great spiritual power and mastery of supernatural faculties,
traveling through the ten directions to serve all the Buddhas.
He constantly employs loving speech and gentle words,
benefiting others through shared activities, and tames sentient beings;
toward all beings, he is like a compassionate father.
The mind and intention are as vast and expansive as the great ocean;
they embrace all sentient beings without exception and are capable of bearing the burden of immeasurable weight.
Out of compassion for suffering sentient beings, he bestows upon them peace and security.
If any sentient beings come to him seeking something,
he accords with their wishes and does not oppose their intentions.
To those who seek official rank, he grants office and noble title;
to those who seek great wealth, he bestows a treasury of jewels;
to those who are ill, he grants peace and security.
If any kings desire to fulfill their wishes,
I shall grant them all without contradicting their intentions;
if they seek long life, I shall grant them long life.
I wish to cause the land to be free from calamities,
so that rain falls in its proper season, neither too dry nor too flooded,
hitting the perfect balance and being free from all disasters such as frost.
Grain and rice will be abundant, the people will be peaceful and happy,
pestilence and toxins will not prevail,
and all their wishes will be fulfilled without ever being thwarted.
At that time, the king was further able to recite the dharani phrases previously explained; moreover,
he transformed the people through the ten wholesome paths of action,
cultivating merit just as I have described above.
That king should likewise practice in this manner.
Having attained such practice, he should further recite this dhāraṇī;
thereby, the extremely heavy evil karma committed in past kalpas will be purified.
All were completely extinguished without remainder.
At that time, once the king’s karmic defilements had been eliminated,
his mind became serene and free from all afflictions and sufferings.
They regard enemies and loved ones with equanimity, harboring no partiality.
They regularly bathe and observe the fast on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days of the month.
At the clear dawn, before the Sun King has yet risen, they perform their rites.
Whether in a main hall or atop a high tower,
sit facing due east and recite this dhāraṇī mantra seven times.
Having burned white sandalwood and aloeswood incense and scattered flowers of seven colors as an offering to the Buddhas of the ten directions,
one should then recite my name three times: "Oṣadhipati Nāgarāja, fulfill my wishes!"
Thus he spoke three times.
He then immediately recited these dharani phrases seven times before ceasing.
At that time, because the king had already been sincere and earnest, [the deity appeared].
The Buddhas of the ten directions and the great Bodhisattvas;
Śakra, Brahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings;
and the eight Great Dragon Kings, including myself, the Dragon King Utpala.
He covers his land with the canopy of loving-kindness and compassion;
he sprinkles his realm with the water of ambrosia,
causing all diseases, pestilential poisons, and noxious vapors to be completely extinguished.
This is called the great divine mantra-power that fulfills vows without fail.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva,
I wish to speak of the four great vows.
What are the four?
First, to shelter and nourish all sentient beings,
like a bridge or boat that ferries people across without weariness.
Second, may I encompass all things like the great void.
Third, may my body be like a medicinal tree,
such that whoever hears of it shall have all their afflictions and sufferings completely eliminated.
Fourth, may it be my vow that when I attain Buddhahood in the future,
the sentient beings I deliver shall be as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River;
this is the bodhisattva’s mind of vast salvation.

“Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva, I wish to joyfully explain the four matters concerning the pure and wondrous practices cultivated by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas for the purification of their buddha-fields. What are these four?”
First, sacrificing one's own benefit for the sake of others to rescue and deliver all living beings;
second, not giving rise to grief or distress when faced with gain or loss, praise or blame;
third, maintaining purity and abstaining from lust, so that one’s precepts and conduct are as pure as a white lotus flower.
Fourth, when I attain Buddhahood in a future age,
all sentient beings within my land shall achieve such sublime conduct that there will be no distinction between humans and devas.
This constitutes the pure and wondrous practice for the adornment of a bodhisattva’s buddha-field.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva further desired to explain it:
"Bodhisattvas have four methods of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*). What are these four?"
First, the Bodhisattva practices the six pāramitās while simultaneously transforming others and rescuing all beings.
Second, he gives rise to a mind of compassion to nurture and sustain all living creatures.
Third, benefiting oneself and others, thereby benefiting both self and other.
Fourth, regarding those who suffer from illness with a heart of compassion, as if looking upon an only child.
These are the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) by which a bodhisattva gathers in sentient beings.
Bodhisattvas extensively benefit sentient beings,
gathering and embracing the wondrous and virtuous merits of the pure lands;
Bodhisattva Jyotirvikrāntagāmin further desires to joyfully explain this.
There are four great vows not shared with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
What are the four?
First, may my mind be like the great earth.
All grasses, trees, thickets, and sprouts grow because of it,
yet the earth feels neither hatred nor affection;
second, may my mind be like a bridge or a boat.
I shall ferry sentient beings across without weariness or fatigue.
Third, I vow that my mind may be like the great ocean,
receiving and containing all the rivers of the hundred streams.
Fourth, may my body be like empty space, encompassing all things just as the *dharmatā* does.
These are the four great vows of a bodhisattva.
This is not shared with the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
Bhadrapāla, I wish to joyfully proclaim that there are eight matters concerning the sublime conduct of a bodhisattva.
What are the eight?
First, when a bodhisattva dwells in a world of five corruptions,
they rescue sentient beings without giving rise to weariness or fatigue.
Second, seeing sentient beings undertake meritorious deeds,
one provides protection and assistance without giving rise to a defiled mind.
Third, seeing people commit evil, one earnestly exhorts and admonishes them so that they may abandon it.
Fourth, when there are those facing peril, he rescues and pities them as a mother loves her child.
Fifth, when there are those who come seeking help, he does not spare even his own body or life.
Sixth, when there are those in places of danger, he assists and escorts them, enabling them to escape the peril.
Seventh, seeing those with wrong views, they feel compassion for them and earnestly exhort them so that they may attain right view.
Eighth, they nurture all sentient beings as if they were their own infants,
dedicating all their merits to them.
Dedicating this merit in common toward unexcelled bodhi—
these are the eight matters by which a bodhisattva benefits immeasurable sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta further desired to speak with joy.
A bodhisattva has four matters by which they benefit sentient beings with a mind free from weariness.
What are these four?
First, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva personally relinquishes his own happiness to bestow it upon sentient beings.
Seeing others suffer, he regards it as no different from his own;
his compassionate heart flows with such pity that its pain penetrates to the very marrow of his bones.
Second, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva establishes great bridges and ships at places of drowning,
ferrying sentient beings across without weariness or fatigue.
Third, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva [acts for] sentient beings who are circling and turning back within the ocean of birth and death.
Fourth, knowing that all sentient beings throughout the past and present are like illusions and transformations,
one reaches this principle yet never tires of delivering others.
These are the four matters by which a bodhisattva benefits and rescues sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta further desires to speak with joy on this subject.
"Whoever is able to perform the work of a Buddha within the bequeathed Dharma of Śākyamuni Buddha, we eight shall constantly protect them.
Briefly stated, there are four matters; what are these four?"
First, there are immeasurable billions of sufferings;
seeing the suffering of sentient beings as no different from one's own.
Second, the merit of the precepts we uphold.
They give everything away as a gift to sentient beings,
dedicating it together for the sake of unsurpassed bodhi;
third, they are able to endure painful matters.
Fourth, they bear the burden of all sentient beings to the further shore;
they rouse the minds of all sentient beings,
just as a compassionate father thinks of his children without distinction.
This constitutes the pure and sublime conduct by which a bodhisattva benefits both themselves and others.
The Bodhisattva Firm Courage (Dṛḍhavīrya) further desired to joyfully proclaim that there are four matters concerning the sublime conduct of a bodhisattva.
What are the four? First,
may I always be born in worlds where no Buddha resides,
just as the sun and moon travel across Jambudvīpa.
First, to remove their darkness;
second, like using a golden probe to pierce the film over the eyes so that they may behold the light;
third, to act as a great medicinal tree for all sentient beings.
Those who smell this fragrance have their suffering and illness eliminated.
Fourth, he constantly expounds the Dharma like a downpour of the rain of Dharma,
causing sprouts to grow and mature into fruit.
They all resolve upon the unsurpassed mind of bodhi.
These are the four great vows of the Bodhisattvas.
I, Mañjuśrī, now wish to speak these sublime verses.
May this sutra be circulated so that sentient beings may have no doubts;
the profound and wondrous Dharma taught by the assembly of the seven Buddhas and bodhisattvas,
and the speech of the devas, nāga kings, and spirits, are most extraordinary.
This is the spell of the Pure and Wondrous Conduct.

For those who write it down, read it, and recite it to protect the nation and the practitioner, they will surely join the assembly of the thousand Buddhas and the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha. Now I wish to speak half a verse.
Praise be to the scribe, and to those who copy, read, and recite this teaching of the noble ones of antiquity! Praise be to the one who transmits it;
their words are concise, beautiful, exquisite, and inexhaustible.
Just as the waters of the great ocean are deep and vast, beyond measure or end,
so too the merit of this person exceeds that by a hundred millionfold.
I, Mañjuśrī, now wish to speak a verse.
Among all classes of sentient beings, none are able to awaken from the surging waves of the realm of lustful ghosts; only I can rescue them,
forever severing the root of birth and death, so that they may universally abide in the bliss of nirvana.
The two verses spoken by Brahmādeva:
Now having come here, I hear these wondrous words: "I have constantly practiced the four immeasurables;
Now having come here, I hear these wondrous words: To deliver sentient beings from the suffering of birth and death."
Forever free from further anxiety, distress, and affliction, the King of the Tuṣita Heaven now wishes to speak three verses:
"In the past, I encountered various Buddhas And attained rebirth in Tuṣita as a Heavenly King.
Now that I have heard this one wondrous word, The film of my mind is pierced through and the eye of wisdom opened."
Should there be sentient beings who hear this but once with their ears, they shall not fall into the three miserable realms but ascend to the Brahma Heaven.
The King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven wished to speak half a verse,
yet he heard that in this Jambudvīpa there were great bodhisattvas and the like.
He expounded the subtle and profound meaning, and my heart was filled with great joy;
the seeds of birth and death were forever uprooted, and I attained entry into the Hall of Nirvana.
This is the second and a half verses spoken by the Heavenly King Sunirmita.
I have heard that throughout Jambudvīpa, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas each proclaim wondrous practices,
the four means of integration, and their great vows;
having heard these words, the eyes of my mind have opened wide.
May all the hosts of devas obtain this pure faculty of the eye,
forever severing the stream of birth and death, and universally attain entry into Nirvāṇa.
Then King Yama of the Yāma Heaven, wishing to speak two verses like a wish-fulfilling jewel, said:
"We have long dwelt in the celestial palaces, weary of the suffering of birth and death within the three realms.
When shall we be like a snake shedding its old skin, forever attaining the bliss of quiescent nirvana?
Thus did the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven wish to speak one and a half verses.
Having long dwelt within birth and death, Weary of and renouncing the mire of desire,
He gave rise to great compassion To rescue and deliver others from the suffering of birth and death;
Forever liberated from the suffering of birth and death, He attained entry into the city of Nirvāṇa.
The Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra wished to speak these four verses:
"Among the Four Great Heavenly Kings, I am the foremost;
though I am a heavenly king, I have not escaped the suffering of ghosts and spirits."
I have been a king of the ghost spirits for five hundred years;
constantly roaming to the east and west, I deliver all living beings.
Alas! In past lives, I was once a king among men.
If you govern and transform others without principle, you will now become a king of ghosts.
May all kings of nations have this vow: govern state affairs with rectitude and do not engage in acts of greed or corruption;
otherwise, you shall again receive the body of a ghost.
The Heavenly King Virūpākṣa wished to speak one and a half verses:
"I recall my past lives when I was born in Jambudvīpa as a wealthy man with sovereign power, yet I was deceitful and not upright."
Although I am now a king of ghosts and spirits, I still undergo the suffering of ghosts and spirits.
The Heavenly King Virūḍhaka wished to speak three verses:
"Now that I act as a king of ghosts and spirits, I have attained liberation from the sufferings of the three miserable realms."
Having traveled throughout the four continents to rescue those suffering from illness, he now recalls his past lives:
once a king among the gods, he was heedless and attached to the five desires; thus, he has now received the body of a ghost-king.
Furthermore, may the king among men, being prudent and free from negligence,
deliver all sentient beings so that they may universally attain the bliss of nirvāṇa.
King Vaiśravaṇa then wished to recite three verses.
In the past, I cultivated enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings by acting as a king of ghosts.
Because sentient beings have long dwelt in the darkness of ignorance, I used a golden scalpel to open their eyes;
once the eye of wisdom was opened, they were delivered from birth and death, and having escaped birth and death, they ascended to Nirvana.
The Nanda Dragon King wished to speak two and a half verses:
"I now dwell within the dragon palace, Desiring to deliver the multitude of dragons;
Having heard of the assembly of Bodhisattvas, Each shall speak of their wondrous conduct."
All the devas, nāgas, and spirits listen with their ears pricked;
the hosts of devas and nāgas are filled with such joy that they cannot contain themselves.
I and my entire retinue have been liberated from the bodies of nāgas.
The Nāga King Pāṇṇada now wishes to speak one and a half verses:
"Abiding here in the nāga palace, Like a silkworm within its cocoon,
I pray for the power of wisdom To destroy this darkness of ignorance."
Rescuing all from calamities and hardships, Transcending the ocean of birth and death.
The Nāga King Sāgara wished to speak two verses:
"I recall a past life, When I once served as a king among men."
Those who were stingy with their treasuries now receive the bodies of dragon kings;
may all kings of nations instead exercise universal compassion and salvation,
governing and transforming through the True Dharma, and never again receive the bodies of dragons.
The Naga King Vasuki wished to speak two and a half verses:
"Though I have received a naga body, I do not suffer the pain of hot sand.
Furthermore, in a past life, I once served as a king among men."
Having been greedy, corrupt, and attached to worldly pleasures, you now receive the body of a dragon king. Furthermore,
may all kings grow weary of and renounce worldly pleasures,
as a prisoner loathes his prison, and transcend the gates of the three realms.
The Naga King Takṣaka wished to recite two and a half verses:
"Furthermore, in the past, I was once a king among men;
my wives, children, and even my servants and slaves—I gave them all away as gifts."
Because of a single act of anger while seated, you now receive the body of a dragon king.
Furthermore, I pray that all kings will be humble and respectful through benevolence and righteousness,
and no longer pride themselves on their own nobility, lest they later receive the body of a dragon king.
The Nāga King Anavatapta wished to speak four verses:
"I recall in a past life, having been the daughter of a king in Jambudvīpa,
my beauty was peerless and without equal."
The father king cherished him deeply; his name was Pundarika.
He was married to the king of a neighboring kingdom, but failing to satisfy her wishes, she became consumed by rage, took her own life, and underwent the sufferings of the three miserable realms.
Now you have received the body of a nāga king; furthermore,
may all women grow weary of their female form, never again harbor jealousy,
and thus avoid suffering as venomous dragons in the future, from which it is difficult to escape when the time of suffering arrives.
The Nāga King Manasvin now wishes to speak two and a half verses:
"Having long dwelt in the nāga palace, I am weary of the stench and filth of the nāgas,
Like a pig in a sty, Or one dwelling in a latrine who feels no pain."
All the humans and devas within the three realms are likewise thus;
they take pleasure in the prison of the three realms as a pig does not loathe its latrine.
Alas, how deeply pitiable! They do not know to seek liberation.
The Naga King Utpala now wishes to speak five and a half verses:
"In a past life, I was once the son of a brahmin family in Jambudvīpa;
I was intelligent and possessed of great wisdom."
At that time, there was a king of a neighboring country whose daughter came to marry my wife.
This woman was not chaste; she had a secret affair with another man.
When I spied upon her and caught them, I had her executed in the marketplace.
At that time, those wicked thieves sent him back to his own country;
reflecting upon the foulness and impurity [of sensual desires], he left the household life to practice the Right Path.
Yet, he again encountered evil associates and failed to meet with virtuous companions.
I lured many lecherous men there; at that time, I lamented in grief and regret, taking a blade to cut my own throat and die.
Having endured the sufferings of the three miserable realms, I have since received this dragon body—its extreme agony is beyond description.
The Nāga King Hūsudīra now wishes to report one matter:
regarding the sixteen kingdoms of Jambudvīpa that I govern,
the other countries are all easy to convert, yet this particular country alone is difficult to teach.
The ministers are all sycophantic and hypocritical; they are greedy, corrupt, and full of treachery and guile.
Droughts and floods occur without regularity—all of which arises from these matters.

One Chapter from the Amitābha-Dundubhisvararāja-dhāraṇī Sūtra. Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at the Kakutthā Pond in the great city of Campā,
together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus.
I shall now expound for you the Western World of Peace and Bliss.
There currently resides a Buddha named Amitābha.
If there are members of the fourfold assembly who can correctly receive and uphold the name of that Buddha, [they shall attain rebirth there].
By virtue of this merit, at the time of their impending death,
Amitābha, together with his great assembly,
will go to that person’s side and cause them to behold him.
Having seen this,
he immediately gave rise to joy and his merit increased manifold.
By virtue of these causes and conditions, wherever he was born...
Forever free from the defiled form of the womb and sensual desire,
they are spontaneously born amidst pure and exquisite jewel lotus flowers,
endowed with great supernormal powers and a brilliant, radiant splendor.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
all together praised that Land of Peace and Bliss,
saying that all the Buddha-dharma therein is inconceivable.
The various skillful means manifested through supernormal powers are inconceivable.
If there are those who can believe in such matters,
one should know that such persons are themselves inconceivable.
The karmic retribution thus obtained is also inconceivable.
Amitābha Buddha, together with his śrāvakas,
is a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
The name of that country was Qingtai (Pure Peace).
The city where the Sage King resided measured ten thousand yojanas in length and breadth,
and it was filled with members of the Kṣatriya caste.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitābha’s father was named Candraśūro-rāja, a Wheel-Turning Sage King;
his mother was named Viśeṣacārumukhī.
His son was named Candraprabha (Moonlight), who served him with devotion;
his disciple was named Vimalakīrti (Stainless Renown) for his wisdom;
another disciple was named Bhadrapāla (Virtuous Light); and one renowned for his diligence in supernatural powers was named Mahāvikurvaṇa (Great Transformation).
At that time, there was a Māra named Ajita.
Among them was one named Devadatta, who was called Śānta.
Amitābha Buddha was together with sixty thousand great bhikṣus.
If there are those who uphold the name of that Buddha,
firming their minds so as to remember it without forgetting,
and for ten days and ten nights relinquish all distraction;
Diligently cultivate and collect the *nien-fo san-mei* (Buddhānusmṛti-samādhi).
Know that the Tathāgata eternally and constantly dwells in the Land of Peace and Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
Maintain this mindfulness continuously, never allowing it to be interrupted.
One should receive, uphold, read, and recite this Great Dhāraṇī of the King of Drum-Sounds;
for ten days and ten nights, during the six periods, one should focus the mind exclusively upon it,
prostrating with the five limbs touching the ground to pay homage to that Buddha.
With firm right mindfulness, one completely eliminates all distraction.
If one can cause the mind to flow without interruption from moment to moment,
one will certainly behold that Amitābha Buddha within ten days.
They also see the Tathāgatas of the worlds in the ten directions and their respective abodes;
except for those with heavy obstructions and dull faculties who,
at this present moment, are unable to behold them.
Dedicate all roots of goodness without exception,
vowing to attain rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
On the day of your passing, Amitābha Buddha...
Together with the great assembly, he appeared before that person, comforting them and praising their excellence.
At that moment, the person felt profound joy;
by virtue of these causes and conditions, they immediately attained rebirth according to their aspiration.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"What is called the Great Dhāraṇī of the King of Drum-Sounds?
I shall now explain it; listen well."
"Yes, we shall receive your instruction. At that time, the World-Honored One spoke the mantra, saying:

If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās,
they should always with utmost sincerity receive, uphold, read, recite, and practice according to the teaching.
Those who practice this dhāraṇī-dharma should dwell in a secluded and quiet place.
Bathe the body and don new, clean garments;
consume white, plain food and abstain from wine, meat, and the five pungent herbs, while constantly practicing the pure conduct (*brahmacarya*).
Offer fine incense and flowers in worship to the Tathāgata Amitābha.
And to the Buddha’s place of enlightenment and the assembly of great bodhisattvas;
one should always thus single-mindedly fix the mind upon them,
making a vow to seek rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

These fifteen spirits constantly roam the world,

These various spirits and ghosts possess terrifying forms;

they cause all children to give rise to fear and dread.

Mi-chou-ka (Mīcuka) has a form like that of an ox; Mi-jia-wang (Mīkārāja) has a form like that of a lion; Qian-tuo (Khaṇḍa) has a form like that of the god Kumāra; A-po-xi-mo-luo (Apasimara) has a form like that of a wild fox; Mou-zhi-ka (Mucika) has a form like that of a monkey; Mo-zhi-ka (Macika) has a form like that of a rākṣasī; Sha-mi-ka (Śamika) has a form like that of a horse; Jia-mi-ni (Kāminī) has a form like that of a woman; Li-po-di (Ripati) has a form like that of a dog; Fu-duo-na (Pudana) has a form like that of a pig; Man-duo-nan-ti (Mandānandi) has a form like that of a cat; She-jiu-ni (Śakunī) has a form like that of a crow; Gan-tuo-bo-ni (Kaṇṭhapuṇī) has a form like that of a rooster; Mu-qie-man-duo (Mukhamanda) has a form like that of a jackal; Lan-po (Lambā) has a form like that of a snake.
These fifteen spirits afflict young children, causing them to tremble with fear.
I shall now further describe the signs of fear in children when they are possessed by these spirits:
when possessed by the Mīchuka spirit, the child’s pupils roll about.
A child possessed by the Miga-rāja spirit repeatedly vomits;
one possessed by the Khanda spirit has both shoulders twitching;
and one possessed by the Apasmāra spirit has foam issuing from the mouth.
When possessed by the Mucilinda spirit, the child clenches its fists and cannot unclench them;
when possessed by the Mucilinda spirit, the child bites its own tongue;
when possessed by the Jambuka spirit, the child delights in weeping and laughing.
When possessed by the Kāminī spirit, the child delights in women;
when possessed by the Līpadi spirit, the child manifests various mixed signs;
when possessed by the Pūtana spirit, the child is terrified and weeps while asleep.
When possessed by a Mandanati spirit, a child cries and laughs excessively;
when possessed by a Śakuni spirit, a child refuses to drink milk;
when possessed by a Khaṇḍapāni spirit, the child’s throat becomes congested and their voice is choked.
The child possessed by the demon Mūka-maṇḍa suffers from fever, heat, and diarrhea;
the child possessed by the demon Lambā frequently belches and frequently hiccups.
These are the fifteen demons.

one shall cause the donor to obtain unconditioned loving-kindness (*maitrī*).
Entering the profound Dharma-gate, they attain supreme, perfect enlightenment.
Their conduct is like that of a bodhisattva, and their realization of the Way is like that of a Buddha, extensively delivering all beings.
The Buddha spoke this text on the Vessel for Incantations, saying: "O Venerable Bhikṣu," the Buddha said.
He takes pity on those within the five realms of existence throughout the ten directions;
he establishes them as fields of merit and as true vessels for the Dharma.
When covered, he is like the heavens; when looked up to, he is like the ocean.
May all beings be blessed and provided for by everything;
may the great deity who enters the Vinaya protect them,
ensuring that ghosts and spirits cannot approach or violate them.
If one offers a bowl— whether it be large or small, beautiful or ugly,
coarse or fine— without giving rise to thoughts of joy or anger,
the act of placing it into the vessel immediately generates great merit.
Thus, the paths to the three miserable realms are closed and the gates to the three liberations are opened.
The giver gains merit and the recipient attains peace and security.
Those who consume this food possess the precepts and are complete in merit.
May this food be transformed into the medicine of the Dharma, so that all may receive deliverance.
The Buddha spoke the incantation for the mendicant’s staff, saying: "Now, O Venerable Bhikṣu, you shall have a heart of compassion for all sentient beings."
Desiring to bring peace to all beings, one should fashion a *khakkhara* staff with three sections;
by directing the mind upward, it restrains the three poisons,
establishes the Three Vehicles, and leads one to enter the gateways of the three liberations of the Unsurpassed.
The twelve great deities who enter the Vinaya descend and submit to provide protection.
This is the Dharma-staff of the True Person;
it brings peace and security to the three realms and guides all beings so that they may attain liberation.
The Buddha Spoke on the Text for the Recitation of Mantras While Seated Alone. The Buddha said: "Now, Venerable Bhikṣu, you have established purity.
You have newly prepared this seat, the *niṣīdana*.
The Great Devas of the Higher Realms shall protect this seat."
Do not allow ghosts or spirits to recklessly approach or defile this seat.
This seat, when donned once,
shall pacify the three realms, bring security to the three periods of time, and thereby bring peace to all sentient beings.
Sitting as if there were originally no seat and being unattached to anything, all are at peace.
Widely delivering all living beings so that they may attain right concentration with an unshakable mind—
this is the seat by which one swiftly accomplishes the unsurpassed, true, and correct path.

Svāhā. When practicing this dhāraṇī rite,
one should use white, pure cotton cloth or fine linen to fashion an image of Avalokiteśvara.
Clad in white robes and seated upon a lotus flower,
he holds a lotus in one hand and a water flask in the other,
with his hair standing erect.
Perform this practice before an image of Avalokiteśvara from the eighth to the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight,
wearing fresh, clean garments and smearing the ground with cow dung.
Furthermore, one should smear fragrant clay over its surface.
With a mind of deep reverence, one should fill twelve vessels with fresh milk and four earthenware vessels with fine incense— indeed, the finest incense possible.
Sixteen strings of flowers, sixteen earthen lamps,
black and solid aloeswood incense,
and four large earthen jars filled with pure water are required.
Place various kinds of flowers within the vessel and kindle fire with wood from milky trees.
Furthermore, one must recite the dhāraṇī while holding eight hundred lotus flowers.
One should cause the sound to continue in succession so that the virtuous mind is not interrupted.
Recite the mantra once and cast one flower into the fire each time.
At that moment, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will come from the east.
A great divine light manifested, blazing upon the fire.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara appeared within the flames exactly like the painted image:
his body was clad in white robes and his hair stood upright.
Holding a flower in his hand, he appears amidst the flames;
when one sees him, no fear arises in the mind.
One should know that such a person immediately closes the gates to the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals.
Whatever they desire or seek, they shall obtain it all.
Whether they seek to become noble, or seek to fly through the air,
or wish to bestow gifts upon sentient beings, they will act with sovereign mastery according to their will.
They shall all obtain it.
Whether they seek extensive learning, seek debate,
seek entry into the profound, or seek hidden treasures.
One who seeks to partake of the elixir of the immortals; one who seeks exquisite beauty;
one who seeks ox-gallstone (gaurika);
one who seeks the divine eye; and one who seeks the divine ear.
It extinguishes all ailments and pains.
Whether one’s body or sensory faculties are incomplete,
or if one suffers from leprosy or any other form of illness and suffering.
Even those whose bodies and sense faculties were incomplete shall all be healed and restored,
and they shall also be cleansed of all heavy karmic burdens from the past.
If a man desires a woman's body or a woman desires a man's body,
they shall all obtain it according to their wishes; once their request has been fulfilled,
they should return [the body] to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.

The Avalokiteśvara-spharaṇa-puṣpa-pūjā-pratītyasamutpāda-dhāraṇī: Namo rakṣa-risaye | Namo 'ritha | Varo-citi | Śaphara-saye | Bodhisattva-saye | Mahāsattva-saye | Tathāgata | Kiri | Kiri | Jiri | Jiri | Śūlu | Śūlu | Gaca | Gaca | Sayatā-śūṇi | Arisaya | Varociti | Śaphara-saye | Svāhā. One should take a handful of fine flowers.
Recite this dhāraṇī three times and scatter it at the feet of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, burn fine incense as an offering.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva suddenly vanished from sight.

[He had taught] the *Dhāraṇī for the Extinction of Sins and the Fulfillment of Wishes*: *Namo lecang li she she | namo ali she | balu jidi | shafuo lishi | pusa tisha | mohe sata sha | ta zhi da | dou liu | dou liu | asi | mo si | molini | diba molini | dou dou pi | namo namo | svāhā.* To practice this *dhāraṇī* rite, one should burn aloeswood incense before an image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and perform repentance with a sincere heart.
Reciting this dhāraṇī three times can extinguish all karmic offenses from beginningless time and bring about great merit;
whatever one seeks or desires will surely be attained according to one's wishes.

Recite the mantra over the enchanted grass one hundred and eight times.
If there are any deficiencies in the sense faculties,
or if there are missing parts such as the hands, feet, ears, eyes, or nose.
By rubbing it with enchanted grass, one can,
through the power of the incantation, protect them all and cause them to recover;
it can bring everything to fulfillment.

The Dhāraṇī for Healing Fever Spoken by Avalokiteśvara: Namo leran liśe śe | Namo ariśe | Varuṇiśe | Śavaraśe | Bodhisattvaśe | Mahāsattvaśe | Tadhyata | Culi | Mahāculi | Ukṣi mukṣi | Sambhṛṅga | Mahāsambhṛṅga | Sambhṛti | Mahāsambhṛti | Aṅgasi | Paṅgasi | Gasi | Gasi | Mahāgasi | Gacchasele | Muktu duse | Svāhā || This is the ritual method for this dhāraṇī incantation.
Whether using a thread, water, or grass, recite the mantra three times;
then, if using a thread, tie it; if using grass, stroke with it; if using water, sprinkle it.
By this means, all febrile illnesses shall be cured and eliminated in the space of a single thought-moment.

The Dhāraṇī Spoken by Avalokiteśvara for Eliminating All Insanity and Malevolent Ghosts: Namo lecang li she she | Namo ali she | Parakiti | Śavara she | Bodhisattva she | Mahāsattva she | Tadātve | Cili | Micili | Rakṣa rakṣa mo ali she | Parakiti | Śavara she | Svāhā. This dhāraṇī can eliminate all diseases of insanity.
If one is seized or afflicted by any kind of *piśāca*, ghost, or spirit,
tie three knots with thread of five colors,
recite the mantra over them three times, and bind them around the neck of the patient.
All illnesses shall be immediately cured and healed.
If the five colors are unavailable, red thread may also be used.
This is the *dhāraṇī* spoken by Avalokiteśvara for removing various fears: *Namo le nang li shé shé*.
Namo Aḷivaruṇadevasya.
Bodhisattva mahāsattva tathāgata.
Mukhya-mukhya-cchedanaṃ kuru.
Vicitrāṅgavimalagarbheśvararājeśvara.
Svāhā mukhe vimukhe svabhāve.
Paiśunya-saṃbhedaka-pāyattika-paiśunya-rāja-bhikṣuṇī.
Māranava yinjurābaya abiliyin.
Piśāca, Yintan, Situotuo, Yinao,
and Yiniluopo.
Uddakā Rāmaputta, Arada Kālāma,
and Sanjaya Belaṭṭhiputta.
Gadupajura jūḍiśe gadupaśaṅkha jūḍiśe.
Gadupaspigala-judeśa gadupa-rakṣa-judeśa gadupa.
Cibīzhudi shéjiā dūpó zhēndá zhūlì.
Gajudhiśe gatudhva kṣiḥ sañjudhiśe.
Gadupani-gaṇḍa-vibhaṇḍaka-pāṇḍava-pāṇḍava.
Candraprabha-nuṣā-ācāra-jūti-sāgara-dvīpa.
Kṣe-si-ju-zhu-di-she-jiē-dou-po-san-mu-tuo (Kṣe-si-ju-zhu-di-sarpa-ga-tūpa-trinetra)
Rājūḍi-sa-gādu-pakāre-majūḍi-sa.
Gaduba sababisaṃ bihu mukhaḍeti.
Sarvabuddhābhyo namo bhagavatīṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ.
Hu mu zhe ti lei cha mu a li she.
Parugiti śavara sakhetaḥ (or sakheta)
Nikṣi kṣili bikṣili.
Sarvāṇṭakapralaya-īśvara-karmajñapti-mokṣa-nirbhaya-sarpa.
Nisaha!
This dhāraṇī can eliminate and extinguish all the various great fears of the world.
Whenever one encounters various forms of fear,
whether at a place for sitting, lying down, or walking,
or upon water, earth, thread, or the corner of one's own garment—
Recite the mantra three times.
If one ties knots with a thread, make three knots;
if using water or earth, sprinkle them in the four directions.
This immediately removes [the affliction], excluding liberation.

Avalokiteśvara spoke this *dhāraṇī* for removing all swellings: *namo lecana-ri-sa-sa | namo ari-sa | varuṇi-sa | śavara-sa | bodhisattva-sa | mahāsattva-sa | tathāgata | kili-cili | kili-cili | vicili-vi | kili | svāhā*. This is the mantra-dhāraṇī.
If any sentient beings suffer from swellings—
whether they be inflammatory swellings or wind-induced swellings—
if one recites this mantra over oil three times and applies it to the swelling, all such swellings will be immediately cured and eliminated.
The Dharani Spoken by Avalokiteśvara for Eliminating All Physical Pain:
Namo le nang li she she;
namo a li she ba lu ji ti she bu la she.
Bodhisattva mahāsattva tadyathā.
Tirihirihiyu-ryū (帝利希利休流)
Hūlunā śānni naśānni
Sarvaviśeṣābhibhūjñānavimokṣapratilabdha.
Caṇḍa Caṇḍāliputra Ātāpī Vītātapo Kambala.
Āḍaṃbavāhila-śe āpantala-śe.
Maula-dambha-daśuni-dambi-kṛt-palūpa-śīla-ra-kāṅgu-pa.
He-li-dou-lu-jù-pó-shā-lù-tuó-lù-pó-lè-tà-duó-lù-pó.
Cetiyapatha, Cetayava, Sarvagāma, Śami, Vārāśami.
Śamī śamī śamī.
Śamīmaṃ sarvabhiśeḍiśeni.
*Svāhā*. Recite this mantra twenty-one times.
Use it to consecrate either millet oil or sesame oil.
If there are any places on a person's body afflicted by pain or illness, if one consecrates the oil with the mantra and applies it to those spots, they will immediately be healed.

The Dhāraṇī Spoken by Avalokiteśvara for Eliminating Sudden Abdominal Pain: Namo le nang li shé shé | Namo ali shé | Boluojidi | Shēfúluo shé | Pútísàtuó shé | Mahāsattva shé | Duōzhìduō | Jiūzhī | Jiūzhī | Luozhī | Ānásànbótuóniyí | Svāhā. This dhāraṇī.
If a person suddenly suffers from abdominal pain,
one should empower salt water with this mantra three times and have the afflicted person drink it;
the abdominal pain will then be immediately cured.

The Dhāraṇī Spoken by Avalokiteśvara for Removing Poison, Even for Those Already Dead: Namo lecang li she she | Namo ali she | Varuṇi | Śavara she | Bodhisattva she | Mahāsattva she | Tadhyata | Sari sari | Viśari viśari | Sarvaviṣanāśani | Svāhā. This is the dhāraṇī mantra.
If a person is afflicted by poison and is on the verge of death, or has already died,
if one recites this mantra into their ear,
they will immediately recover; even if dead, they shall return to life.

The Dhāraṇī Spoken by Avalokiteśvara for Removing Sudden Illness and Fainting When One Is Unconscious: *Namo le nali śe śe | namo arili śe | varuṅkṣi śe | bodhisattva śe | mahāsattva śe | tadyathā | nimiri nimiri | sarvakilikha nimiri | mokṣaṇi | mukhiṇi | naśani | vinaśani | sthigali | sthagali | svāhā.* This is the dhāraṇī.
If a person suddenly contracts a grave illness and falls into a swoon, losing consciousness and awareness,
one should dye threads with lac and burn black, solid aloeswood incense.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times and bind it to the patient's body;
they will immediately awaken and be cured.

The Dhāraṇī Spoken by Avalokiteśvara for Removing the Five Tongue Defects, such as a Constricted Throat or a Retracted Tongue: *Namo le nang li she she | namo a li she | ba lu ji ti | she bu la she | pu ti sa tva she | ma ha sa tva she | ta che ta | li mi li | li mi li | ka la | li mi li | gan tha li mi li | bi chi li | svāhā.* This dhāraṇī.

If a person’s five sense-faculties are impaired, their throat is constricted, and their tongue is retracted, they should recite this mantra over earth three times and apply it to the painful area; it will immediately be healed.

This is the *dhāraṇī* for removing various types of leprosy and even wounds and sores, spoken by Avalokiteśvara: *Namo lekha-ri-she-she | namo a-ri-she | ba-ro-ki-ti | she-po-lo-she | po-ti-sa-tuo-she | mo-ho-sa-tuo-she | ta-che-ta | shu-mu-chi | pi-mu-chi | hsiu-liu | hsiu-liu | shu-mu-liu | pi-shu-mu-liu | shou-na-ning | pi-shou-na-ning | mo-si-to-po-t’ou | mo-shou-lo-t’ou | mo-pu-ti-po-po-ti | ta-po-shou-sha-t’ou | svāhā.* This is the *dhāraṇī*.
If a person has leprosy—
whether white leprosy or red leprosy—
or madness, gnashing of teeth, or diseases of sores on the body.
If one is wounded or injured by arrows or blades,
by reciting this mantra over soil and applying it to the wound, one will immediately be healed.

Avalokiteśvara spoke this mantra: take soil from the bottom of a stream and blow it [upon the victim] so that the poisonous vapors will not circulate. Dharani: Namo le nang li she she | Namo a li she | Ba lo ki ti | She bu la she | Bo di sa tuo she | Mo ha sa tuo she | Ta che ta | Chi chi pi chi chi | Shou mi li | Zhi mi li | Bi fei san ning | Ni po lan ning | Pi sha she ni | Mo na si | Mo ha mo na si | Bi li chi li | Mo na si | A jia ti pi sha san chu po ni | Ye ta jia ti | Pi sha | Na she ni | Svāhā. This is the dharani mantra.
When applying the medicinal powder made from soil from the bottom of a mountain stream,
one should mix it with *māra* and smear it over [the wound].
Wherever the sound penetrates, the toxic vapors will not spread.

Avalokiteśvara spoke this mantra for medicinal herbs; by taking it, one attains the *dhāraṇī* of hearing once and holding: *Namo lecang li she she | namo ali she | balu jidi | shafuo lashi | puti sata she | maha sata she | duozhiduo | pilili | biluo | zhudi | tishetisheti | podi | poluoni | shuliuduo | tuoluoni miliditi | tuoluoni | svāhā.* Within seven days, this *dhāraṇī*...
Take half a *liang* of the *pāramī-viṇa-gi* medicine;
after seven days have passed, place this medicine in milk,
and subsequently take this medicine again.
When the main meal has been finished and one wishes to eat a meal mixed with milk-rice,
recite this mantra twenty-one times.
Take this incantation and medicine after [meals].
One will be able to retain whatever is heard once and recite a thousand verses daily.

Avalokiteśvara spoke this five-colored *changpu* (achyranthes) incantation; by taking it, one attains the *dhāraṇī* of hearing and retaining without forgetting: *Namo lekang li she she | namo ali she | baluji ti | shafu la she | bodhisattva she | mahāsattva she | tadyathā | qian zhi | funa li | bolu po li | svāhā.* Recite this incantation before an image of Avalokiteśvara.
Burn aloeswood incense and recite this mantra over the white *changpu* root one hundred and eight times.
By consuming it, one will attain the power of hearing and retaining [the teachings] without forgetfulness.

*Namo le nang li she she | namo a li she | ba lu ji ti | she fu la she | pu ti sa tuo she | mo he sa tuo she | ta che ta | zhu ti | zhu ti | ti qi | bi li she | xiu liu mi | xiu liu mi | he he he | xiu liu mi | ju lai nang | xiu liu mi | svāhā.* Recite this mantra before an image of Avalokiteśvara.
Burn aloeswood incense and recite this mantra over black kusha roots one hundred and eight times.
By consuming them, one will attain the power of hearing and retaining all that is taught without forgetting.

*Namo lerang liśeśe | namo arīśe | varuṇakīti | śavaraśe | bodhisattvaśe | mahāsattvaśe | tadyathā | akini | akini mukhe | sumi sumamukhe | viliśe | viliśe | bale | smṛti | sambhavanidhi ri | dhi ri | vidhiri | svāhā.* This mantra should be recited before an image of Avalokiteśvara.
Burn aloeswood incense and recite this mantra over the roots of red calamus seven times.
By ingesting it, one will attain the power of hearing and retaining [the teachings] without forgetting.

*Namo lerang liśeśe | namo arīśe | varuṇi | śavalāśe | bodhisattvaśe | mahāsattvaśe | tadyathā | muni | vimuni | muni | vimuni | lipati | śīlaparāṇi | parṣaṇi | mukhi | bimukhi | militi | vadaṅge | militi | vadaṅge | śūradha | vadaṅge | śūrudha | garāṇi | svāhā.* This mantra [should be recited] before an image of Avalokiteśvara.
Burn aloeswood incense and recite the mantra over the roots of green calamus one hundred and eight times.
By consuming it, one will attain the power of hearing and retaining all teachings without forgetfulness.
*Namo le nang li she she*.
Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya.
Bodhisattva mahāsattva tadyathā.
Rāhanti muhanti kuliśe.

The Dhāraṇī for Eliminating Disease and Regenerating Flesh Spoken by Avalokiteśvara:

Alikṣaśalinī-mogha-alikṣa.

Then, depending on where the ailment lies, bind them upon that painful spot.
Furthermore, one may recite the mantra over soil and apply it as an ointment.
Alternatively, one may grind *bimbā* into powder, place it in water, and drink it;
this will eliminate the disease of "flowing skin" (*pravāhikā*) and restore health.

The Dhāraṇī Spoken by Avalokiteśvara for Healing Red and White Diarrhea: Namo lecang li she she | Namo ali she | Parogiti | Śavara she | Bodhisattva she | Mahāsattva she | Tadhyata | Araṅga | Varasunmo | Sūsūmiti | Vyaraṅga | Dambaraṅga | Naśaraṅga | Vināśaraṅga | Cita cita | Acitaśara | Maśarabdo | Maśura she do | Cita citado | Svāhā. This is the dhāraṇī.
If a person suffers from dysentery with red or white discharge, recite this mantra over soil three times and apply it to the stool; they will be cured.
Avalokiteśvara spoke this dhāraṇī for wiping all painful areas with medicinal grass, whereby they are immediately healed: *namo le nang li she she*.

Citiṭṭha dūsī tiṭṭhāna-yoni.

Svāhā. If a person contracts one of the hundred ailments and their body is in pain,
they should recite this dhāraṇī over grass three times and brush it over the painful area.
All illnesses and pains shall immediately be healed and cured.
Avalokiteśvara speaks this dhāraṇī that fulfills all wishes:
*Namo lecang li she she, namo ali she*.
Vajradhara bodhisattva.

Sarvavidyāpāramitānirdiṣṭa.

Śrīphalaṃ ca mṛdvīkā-mocā-śarkarāḥ.
Śūlarṣabha-labdhi-jñāna-mudrā.
Vadani nandini nandimukhi.
Caṇḍālī Caṇḍālamukhī Padmavatī.
Bhaṭā-mukhi-sudhākī-śūliśa.

Mahāprajāpatī tunda pe sāri madhu sāri.
Sarvasattvānāṃ kṣemaṃ svasti bhavatu.
Sthāne buddha-maṃśe mārāṇām amoghe.
Māra siṃgha-ma-ru-māra si buddha-sa.

Paro-ki-ti-she-fu-lo-she-si-ch'an-dou (Parogitiśavaraśeṣicanda)
Mudrāpāda svāhā. Practice this dhāraṇī rite.
From the eighth day to the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight,
smear the ground with cow dung and place fragrant liquid in a new, high-quality earthenware vessel.
Place milk in a single earthenware vessel.
One must have a lamp, excellent incense, flowers, and a string of garlands.
Fast for three days and bathe three times each day.
One should spread grass upon the ground and recite [the mantra] eight hundred times over the course of seven days before an image of Avalokiteśvara.
One should wear new, clean garments and burn black, solid aloeswood incense.
Reciting this mantra at the three times of day,
one will surely attain auspiciousness and whatever one’s heart desires.
Whether one consecrates water or earth,
ties a thread, or consecrates mustard seeds and burns them,
or consecrates grass— whatever is convenient for one's mind.
It is used to treat bodily illnesses;
by reciting this mantra before meals, all various ailments will be cured.
This is a mantra that fulfills whatever wishes one has in mind.
It should be practiced for seven nights.
This will also cause all the aforementioned mantras to proceed with auspicious success.
This mantra is a "mantra that accords with the mind."
This was spoken by Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Whatever one seeks shall be obtained according to one's wishes,
and all fears can be extinguished.
It can eliminate all suffering from illness,
it can release one from all bonds,
and it can remove all enmity and harm.
It can eliminate all sorcery and poisons;
it can eliminate all febrile diseases;
and it can subdue all enemies and bandits.
It can eliminate the afflictions of mad spirits and demons.
If one wishes to travel afar, one should recite the mantra and tie it to the corner of one’s robe;
this can eliminate all manner of evils.
If one ties dyed threads around the patient's body, there will be no failure in their recovery;
whether one sprinkles water upon them or binds them with black threads, the same result follows.
They are also able to protect themselves and others,
and even those destined for the hells can attain liberation through them.
This is the fundamental vow of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Delivering all sentient beings.
