*Svāhā*. For one month, abandon all worldly affairs.
At the time when the morning star appears, recite this one hundred and twenty times daily.
Constantly seek these three things.
First, one repents of one's own sinful karma from beginningless time.
Second, one vows that the merit one has cultivated shall be shared with all sentient beings.
Third, one constantly prays that the Bodhisattvas of the ten directions who have not yet attained true and perfect enlightenment may swiftly attain it.
If, having attained the Way, you wish to enter nirvana, I pray that you remain long in this world.
At all times, cultivate a mind of making offerings to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, pay special homage to the Bodhisattva Ariṣṭa-kṣetra-garbha.
Wherever one may be, one should establish the mind and bring it to mind;
whatever wish one desires to seek,
if one suffers from a grave illness and cannot obtain medicine, one shall obtain it at will.
If one wishes to repent, one's offenses will be extinguished immediately.
If there are grave offenses, one will obtain the skillful means to extinguish them.
Furthermore, whatever the mind desires to contemplate, one will obtain the skillful means for it.
If there is to be a dream, one will appear in the form and attire of a śramaṇa;
according to what is appropriate, he will manifest and show them the skillful means.
Should there be worldly matters that they wish to undertake, [he will guide them].
If one does not know the skillful means, yet is able to obtain them according to one's aspiration,
and if one can practice in this manner,
one may proceed at will within the six perfections.
One will be able to attain the power of progress and undergo the trial and verification of the fruits of the Way.
If this dhāraṇī can be practiced for one month with body and mind pure,
having relinquished all causal attachments and fetters.
There is no practice of emptiness that does not yield its fruit.
If a person were to recite the names of other bodhisattvas for an entire kalpa,
it would not equal the merit of reciting the name of this bodhisattva and making offerings to him for a single moment.
This dhāraṇī— *vare kare pauṣṇi*— eliminates all transgressions, fulfills all aspirations,
removes obstacles, cures diseases, and leads to the attainment of the fruits of the Path.

Regarding the practice of the *svāhā* rite: on the eighth day of the month,
having purified oneself by bathing and donned new, clean garments, one should cleanse the inner mind and stand before an image of the Buddha or before the *śarīra*.
For seven days and seven nights, one should single-mindedly recollect the Buddha and chant the mantra one thousand times,
without thinking of any worldly evil dharmas.
One should use one hundred and eight knots made from cotton thread.
By using this binding cord to practice together with the assembly,
evil persons will not see one's form, and while sleeping, one will have no evil dreams.
With a single mind recollecting the Buddha, one shall attain the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
They shall certainly attain the fruit of the unsurpassed path and be revered by all humans and devas,
protected by the Four Great Heavenly Kings.
They eliminate the karma of all three obstructions.
While lying down or asleep, they behold the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions,
and they hear all the teachings they have never heard before.
Free from the four hundred and four diseases,
they are able to heal all the ailments and sufferings of sentient beings and bestow all happiness upon them.

Having attained all the dhāraṇīs of the gates of dhyāna, samādhi, and all Buddha-dharmas: *Omumuni* (O-mu-mu-ni), *Pralumuni* (Po-lo-mu-ni), *Kauśadhe* (Jiu-sha-she-xie), *Kuśivajra* (Jiu-xi-ba-she), *Aparāmṛśa* (A-po-luo-mu-sha), *Sannividha-rahasmi-ti* (Sa-ni-pi-tuo-luo-si-mi-di), *Kātyapāli* (Jia-duo-jia-bo-li), *Bindhujani* (Pin-tou-zhu-ni), *Sārakīramaramati* (Sa-lo-qi-luo-mo-luo-mo-di), *Udithi-anusithi* (You-ti-di-a-nu-si-ti-di), *Sarvarāgamanasini-ti* (Sa-po-rang-mang-lu-na-si-na-di), *Vidhyamati* (Bi-tuo-she-mo-di), *Vindhyamati* (Bi-tou-mo-di), *Suparaditi-ti* (Xiu-bo-luo-di-ti-di), *Anirakṣāpali* (A-ni-luo-xie-a-po-ling), *Cūḷanīmimati* (Chu-luo-ni-mi-mi-di), *Hāsvamūṣi* (He-sa-mu-shi). *Svāhā*. Practice this dhāraṇī method.
If one recites [the mantra] a thousand times before an image of the Buddha or before the śarīra for seven days, drinking a beverage of black honey and lotus flower garlands,
one will be able to recite a thousand verses in a single day and attain the knowledge of others' minds.
If there are members of the fourfold assembly who, in a place of tranquility,
practice this dhāraṇī according to the Dharma with a sincere mind,
they shall attain the four dhyānas within no more than seven days.
Having destroyed the fetters of the desire realm, they attain the Samādhi of the Ten Directions Buddhas’ Sovereign Realization,
which can eliminate the karmic actions of the three obstructions of sentient beings and can incinerate all the fetters of sentient beings' afflictions, inversions, and the like.
By drawing near to and dwelling in the path of the noble ones,
one ensures that there shall be no regression from bodhi and attains omniscience without depending on external causes.
One thereby attains the dharma-gate of the three kinds of unhinderedness, the three kinds of fearlessness, and samādhi of all Buddhas,
which can eliminate all evils of sentient beings.
One beholds all Buddhas through the dhāraṇī-ḍhāka of fulfilling all wishes from the mind.

Svāhā! When the Buddha spoke this dhāraṇī,
the trichiliocosm shook in six ways,
and the devas performed celestial music in the sky.
Various kinds of fragrant flowers and precious jewels rained down as offerings to the Buddha,
the Bodhisattvas, and the great assembly.
At that time, ninety-nine billion nayutas of devas and humans resolved their minds upon Bodhicitta.
If sons or daughters of good family, whether ordained or lay, who have resolved upon Bodhicitta,
should write down and recite this dhāraṇī,
the Buddhas of the ten directions will immediately behold such a person.
Hearing them recite and hear their vows and dedications,
[the Buddha] sees this person from afar and gives rise to a heart of joy,
immediately bestowing upon them the prediction that they shall certainly become a Buddha.
If the fourfold assembly, for the sake of seeking the Buddha-way,
should purify their minds, bathe, don new and clean robes,
and arrange various pure seats.
In a forest hermitage, he remains far removed from the clamor of worldly people;
his mind is untainted by the afflictions of greed and hatred,
and he is free from the thoughts of arrogance, envy, and jealousy.
Constantly maintaining right mindfulness of the Buddhas of the ten directions as if they were before one's eyes,
one should repent of all transgressions three times during the day and night and recite this dhāraṇī.
During seven days, with a virtuous mind and resolute intent,
one shall see the Buddhas of the ten directions; if one does not see them,
one should again focus the mind without distraction for two weeks, three weeks, or seven days.
Immeasurable Buddhas shall appear before them and preach the Dharma for them,
bestowing upon them the prediction that they shall attain Buddhahood;
all obstructive karmas will be completely extinguished.
Even if one has committed the five heinous crimes, violated the fundamental precepts, or slandered the true Dharma—
such that one cannot see the Buddhas in person— even seeing them in a dream can eliminate immeasurable sins.
Furthermore, by diligently applying oneself with even greater vigor for another three weeks,
one will certainly succeed in seeing all the Buddhas;
this dhāraṇī accords with the minds of the fourfold assembly.
Through diligent effort in accordance with the Dharma, one's aspirations will be fulfilled according to one's heart.
One should cultivate the *nien-fo san-mei* (Buddhānusmṛti-samādhi) dhāraṇī,
the *tuo-tuoluo-duo-tuoluo-ni* (*dhāraṇī*).
Dhāraṇī-dhāraṇī-muni-vaṃbha-saṃniṃ.

*Jñānabuddhi-indri-sa-buddhi svāhā*. Regarding the practice of this rite:
during the eighth month of the second or third lunar month, one should first cultivate the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi* (samādhi of mindfulness of the Buddha) during the bright fortnight.
From the eighth day until the fifteenth,
one should visualize the Buddha seated upon a lotus flower;
this should be done three times each during the day and three times each during the night.
By making offerings of fine incense and flowers,
one will certainly see the Tathāgata seated upon a lotus flower preaching the Dharma;
one will obtain dhāraṇīs and attain mindfulness and wisdom.
With firm resolve in the awakening of the mind, one attains the knowledge of past lives,
up until final parinirvāṇa;
[one masters] all sūtras and all arts and crafts.
One can thus fully encompass all such things as these;
one can attain a pure mind and eliminate [ignorance regarding] the Four Noble Truths.
Why is this? Because this dharma is able to encompass that which is with outflows (*sāsrava*).
Those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this dhāraṇī will never fall into the evil realms in whatever place they are born,
and will always encounter the Buddhas.
In every place of rebirth, they shall always be endowed with the seven treasures;
they shall never be born into lowly or base circumstances.
In every place of rebirth, they shall encounter all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
In every place of rebirth, they shall never forget the bodhicitta;
as they travel through the worlds of the ten directions, they shall constantly behold all Buddhas,
O World-Honored One, and always attain their aspirations.

The Bodhisattva Akṣayamati recited the Dhāraṇī of the Vow of Banners and Canopies: *tadyathā | ni-na-saṃśe | vi-ni-na-pi-mo-pe | kāra-ta-le-khe | bu-dhi-va-su-be | cha-ma-ṭṭhe-pe | a-parā-che | ha-cha-ro-be | a-ja-ma-te | mi-li-śi-li | ta-pi-śa-re | aṅ-ku | ja-da-ni | ja-jha-ra-no-se | a-na-ma-śu-ti-mu-kha-ma-le-che | ku-la-ba-ti | ma-li-ka-ba-che | ba-ba-śa-re | a-bu-dhi-ti | mo-pu-li | śa-ra-to-ke | mi-li-ti-mu-ni | svāhā.* —The Bodhisattva Akṣayamati.
In the presence of the Buddha and amidst the assembly of great bodhisattvas,
he proclaimed this Great Dharani of the Vow of the Banner and Canopy.
If there are sentient beings who can wholeheartedly transcribe and uphold this dharani, [they shall attain liberation].
Constantly practicing meditative concentration for seven days and seven nights,
one should recite this dhāraṇī one hundred thousand times according to the Dharma; thereby,
one will attain great merit, great radiance, and great power.
They shall attain the further shore;
they shall be endowed with extensive learning, wisdom, and eloquence;
and they shall be fully possessed of all the precepts of the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One.
They shall accomplish all great merits;
from heavenly kings and earthly monarchs down to brahmins and householders,
all sentient beings who see them will rejoice and give rise to faith and reverence.
Furthermore, all necessary provisions shall be obtained according to their wishes;
they will be sustained by all Buddhas,
and wherever they are reborn, they will assemble together with the Buddhas.
It can cause all sentient beings to open the eye of wisdom and see all sublime dharmas.

It subdues and pacifies enemies, treats venomous bites, and heals swellings. This *dhāraṇī*: Tadañcitā | Iliri | Pucili | Pulentiha | Rābu | Mulembu | Balembu | Jilebu | Bijilebu | Sidi-bu | Bisidi-bu | Mabidibhu | Usrasadi-bu | Svāhā. This *dhāraṇī*.
If a king raises an army and mobilizes the masses to attack an enemy,
and desires victory when about to enter the enemy's territory,
he should recite the mantra over earth three times and smear it upon his body.
Furthermore, they shall anoint banners, standards, pennants, canopies, drums, horns, musical instruments,
and weapons of war; wherever they turn, they shall be certain to prevail,
causing the enemy host to retreat in safety and without further injury or loss.
If one is bitten by a venomous insect,
or if afflicted by poison, or if there is swelling on the body,
one should recite this mantra and apply clear antimony as an ointment to it.
All were healed and restored.
Homage to Avalokiteśvara, who bestows the power of fearlessness,
whose voice is entirely harmonious and elegant, and who possesses the courageous lion’s roar.
With the pure voice of Great Brahmā and the wondrous Dharma-voice of great compassion,
you are a Great Man among gods and humans; you are able to bestow happiness upon sentient beings,
eliminate the latent tendencies of ignorance, and deliver them across the ocean of birth and death.
Now we take refuge in the Buddha of such great supernatural power.

Thus have I heard: The Great Dharani of the Seven Jewels spoken by the Buddha.
At one time the Buddha was staying at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Monastery.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda: "Receive and uphold this Great Seven-Jeweled Dhāraṇī Mantra.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One spoke it.
Xiadi yeta dai tan, dizhe zhishu luti, boluore, boluo, shichachouna, bicha anan. If there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and practice this dhāraṇī mantra.
Throughout their entire lives,
they are able to cause all enemies and adversaries to rejoice;
fire cannot burn them, and blades cannot wound them.
Water cannot drown them;
nor can they be possessed by ghosts or demons of any kind,
whether they be devas, nāgas, asuras, gandharvas, or even humans and non-humans.
Ānanda, as for these seven-jeweled mantras:
whether one enters into water or fire,
or among enemies and bandits, [they shall provide protection].
If one consumes poison or encounters the effects of sorcery and spells,
one should recite this mantra;
then all fears, such as the bristling of body hair and the like, shall be completely liberated.
Comparing the majestic virtue of Vipaśyin Buddha,
the supernatural power of Śikhin,
and the wisdom of Viśvabhū.
The power of Krakucchanda Buddha,
the precepts of Kanakamuni,
and the merit of Kāśyapa.
Śākyamuni exerts diligence so that all sentient beings may completely eliminate their fears and attain peace and security.
At that time, Ānanda, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
Then the Buddha addressed Ānanda:
I shall now proclaim the Great Samantabhadra Dhāraṇī; you should receive and uphold it.
*Tadyathā*: Ata nata ta mi ta cha kuli kuli taye kuli taye badhi sidhi siddha bamdhi. Ānanda, this is the Great Samantabhadra Dhāraṇī.
It wards off and destroys all weapons, eliminates all enemies and adversaries;
it removes all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and other such fears.
It dispels all fevers, diseases caused by spirits, sorcery, poisons, spells, and the like, including the *vidyādhara* and *pūtana*.
None can ever transgress this mantra of Samantabhadra.
It brings all auspiciousness and goodness wherever a son or daughter of good family may go—
whether upon a path or upon a body of water.
In times of emergency or distress,
one should recollect this mantra; there will be no yakṣas,
nor many piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, or kaṭapūtanas.

Furthermore, there shall be no fear of rākṣasas, piśācas, and the like, nor of water, fire, swords, staves, weapons, calamities, poisons, spells, incantations, or any other evils caused by humans or non-humans.
Ānanda, if there are such fears, terrors, or urgent calamities, one should recite and contemplate this mantra;
none will be able to cause harm or affliction.
Furthermore, Ānanda, if there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this mantra...
Just as the celestial devas, nāgas, spirits, the twenty-eight divisions of humans and non-humans,
and others are unable to transgress or violate this mantra,
so too shall the iron wheel and the vajra wheel inflict suffering and affliction upon them.
May their heads be split into seven pieces—
four cardinal directions, four intermediate directions, above, and below—
and may anyone who conceives an evil thought toward this person have that poisonous mind entirely bound so that it does not arise.
These sons and daughters of good family should skillfully read, recite, uphold, and practice it.

This great divine mantra spoken by the Four Heavenly Kings consists of sixty-six verses: (1) *Raktādhaḥ-piśāca-nāma*, (2) *Kāla-pūtana*, (3) *Mahāpūtana*, (4) *Svāhā*. When reciting the mantra, take three colored threads—yellow, red, and green—and tie twenty-one knots.
First bind the feet, then the waist, and finally the hands.

Recite the names of the subordinate spirits: first, Lulu; second, Mahāphulu; third, Umalehamuta; fourth, Vimahamuta; fifth, Pāṭalāhamuta; sixth, Phuphāhamuta; seventh, Svāhā. For the mantra, use two-colored threads, white and black.
Tie fourteen knots and fasten them around the neck.
For the mute spirits, recite: "1. Kṣubhūlu, 2. Hūhūma, 3. Pāṭarahūhūma, 4. Pāṭarahūhūma, 5. Vimalehūhūma, 6. Hanuhūhūma, 7. Svāhā. The mantra-thread should be yellow, red, or green.
Tie it into thirty-seven knots and fasten them around the neck.
Recite the mantra for the *kṣveḍaka* spirits: *Pītara* (1), *pāpa-pū* (2), *pāpa-pū* (3), *umā-le pāpa-pū* (4), *svāhā* (5). Sprinkle water over this seven times.
Wash the face, wash the left ear, and rinse the mouth, each three times.
Covering the eyes with water, recite the mantra seven times: "Ghost named Jipura (1), Jipopa (2), Jipopa (3), Hunu-jipopa (4), Pāṭala-jipopa (5), svāhā (6). Sprinkle the water over the eyes.
The names of the wrathful spirits are: (1) Phobala, (2) Phobalahu, (3) Phobalahu, (4) Phobalahu, (5) Unuphalahu, (6) Utuhu. Svāhā. (7) Recite this mantra seven times over it all.
The name of the *Bhojana-śuṇḍika* (Vomit-eating) ghost is: 1. Duhu-dhuhu, 2. Onupha, 3. Dhuhonupha, 4. Svāhā.
Recite this mantra seventeen times. The name of the *Anāpāna-dhu* ghost is: 1. Anāpāna-dhu, 2. Anāpāna-dhu, 3. Vimāna-dhu, 4. Svāhā. Recite this mantra seventeen times.

The names of the spirits who obstruct the roots of goodness are: (1) Pūlu-pūlu, (2) Hūhū-māpūlu, (3) Anabhinahūpūlu, (4) Citunāvimohunapūlu, (5) Puanāvimohūpūlu. *Svāhā*. Recite this mantra seven times over water and sprinkle it seven times [over the patient].
The names of the parched and thirsty pretas are: (1) Pāpabhū, (2) Punarbhū-pāpabhū, (3) Anāvina-punarbhu-pāpabhū, (4) Phullata-pāpabhū. Svāhā. Recite this mantra twenty-one times.
Take threads of five colors—blue, yellow, red, white, and black—and tie them into twenty-one knots.

Recite the mantra seven times over saffron, blue pigment, and water: "Eyaṃ svāhā" (1), "Pakṣaṇi-pakṣatānu-pakṣaṇi" (2), "Vimā-pakṣatānu-pakṣaṇi" (3), "Bhūta-pakṣaṇi" (4), "Svāhā" (5). Recite this mantra twenty-one times over the saffron, blue pigment, and water.
Always have the patient face the east and repent before the Buddha Sun-Moon Pure Bright Virtue for seven days,
washing their eyes until the seventh day.

The names of the spirits that cannot be restrained are: 1. Śūśura-prapāma-hu-śūśura; 2. Ānāpāna-śūśura; 3. Vimahana-śūśura; 4. Svāhā. Take three *śēṅ* (sheng) of water, mix it with a small amount of chicken egg yolk and salt.
Recite the mantra three times.
Always have the patient face north and perform three prostrations before the Buddha King of Inner Abundance and Adornment.
Then, take one *sheng* of it for consumption.
Seal the remainder with the syllable *Sūśura*.

[Recite] the names of the ghosts: first, *Hudūra-ekahinana*; second, *Hudūra-apabhu*; third, *Hudūra-apathi*; fourth, *Hudūra-apapupuna*; fifth, *Yamuda-hudūra*; sixth, *Svāhā*. Use thread of seven colors.
Tie twenty-one knots:
first bind the neck, next bind both hands, and finally bind the waist and wrists.

Recite the names of the *rākṣasīs* directly: (1) Śabade, (2) Ābhauhuśabade, (3) Vimauhuśabade, (4) Būlida-huhu-śabade, (5) Āmanu-huhu-śabade, (6) Svāhā. One must use five-colored cotton threads: blue, yellow, red, white, and purple.
Tie twenty-one knots—three times seven—and bind them to the feet, then to the waist, then to the hands, and finally to the neck.
Recite the mantra six times over five *śīrṣas* (measures) of water: "Pāpala-ekahūhunu-pāpala, pāpala-utphullita-pāpala, pāpala-aśatru-pāpala, pāpala-aśabudhu-pāpala, svāhā. [Recite this] three times.
Take a small amount of the yolk of half a chicken egg,
a bit of salt, dust from a beam,
and soot from the bottom of a cauldron.
Boil [the medicine] seven times with one handful each.
After boiling it three times, recite the mantra three times.
At sunrise, wash the ulcer seven times and recite the mantra seven times.
One must not eat the food of the lower ghosts named Humādhu, Uṣāhūhū Humādhu, Anukarpi Humādhu, and Prapara Humādhu. Svāhā. (5)
Recite the mantra over water seven times and have the patient drink it.

For pain in the waist and legs, the name of the demon is: (1) Bhuludupāṭala, (2) Bhuludu, (3) Vimara-bhuludu, (4) Mili-kiri-pi-bhuludu, (5) Svāhā. Recite this over three-colored threads—blue, yellow, and green.
Tie seven knots.
Bind them around the ankles, then the thighs, and finally the waist.

For the headache-demons named: (1) Humadumaha-kāṭara, (2) Vimaka-kaṭara, (3) Bhūbhūra-kaṭara, (4) Ibhū-kaṭara, (5) Imakajika-kaṭara—(6) Svāhā. Recite the mantra twenty-one times and strike the willow branch twenty-one times.

The names of the dark and dull spirits are: 1. Hutāṭa-bhūti; 2. Hutāṭa-ācīna; 3. Hutāṭa-bhūticī; 4. Hutāṭa-ihuparācī; 5. Svamitau-ihucīparā. Svāhā. Recite this mantra twenty-one times for seven days, chanting it three times each day.
The names of the demons who cause earache are: 1. Bini-bha, 2. Ajibhi-bini-bha, 3. Hūni-bhi-bini-bha, 4. Ihuci-bhini-bha, 5. Kimabhi-bhini-bha, 6. Svāhā. On the first day of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa.
If the left ear is painful, sit facing south;
if the right ear is painful, sit facing north. The door shall face east.
The patient sits inside the door, and the mantra-reciter sits outside the door.
One should also recite the mantra over water twenty-one times outside the gate and sprinkle it three times.

The name of the demon who causes rheumatic pain is Pāpala-ekaphuli-phuli (1). Place Pāpala (2). Carmunā-pāpala (3). Huhula-carmapala (4). Kappati-carmapala (5). Svāhā (6). Recite this mantra over the water thirty-five times.
Insert a reed tube into the opening of a water jar.
Recite the mantra seven times over it, spit upon it once at the end, and finally scoop up some water and sprinkle it toward the face.

For urinary obstruction caused by the spirit named Udura—one invocation: *jiliṭa udura*, two invocations: *durāhaṇatīṭa udura*, three invocations: *sāhā*. Take two and a half *sheng* of boiling water from beneath a cooking cauldron.
Mix the yolk of a chicken egg with white honey and have the patient consume it;
sit facing due south.
Recalling the Buddha Candrasūryapradīpa, perform four prostrations seven times.
Inhale [the air] once, as much as half a hen’s egg, and then spit it out.

This will immediately cure those suffering from abdominal pain caused by demons named: (1) Madgura, (2) Aṭanika-madgura, (3) Cippatuniga, (4) Kuhuniga, (5) Abhiliginiga, (6) Cippajiniga, (7) Svāhā. Recite this mantra over water twenty-one times.
First, spit three times; then, inhale the remainder three times.
For the fever-demon named 1. Sumida, 2. Anīta, 3. Kajñīta, 4. Uhunāsumida, 5. Jibahūsumida, 6. Icīṭaṭhasumida, 7. Svāhā—use five-colored threads and perform seven knots while reciting this mantra.
If the pain descends from the head,
first bind the neck, then bind the feet, and then bind the hands.
If it becomes extremely urgent, recite the mantra over water three times and sprinkle it upon the patient.

The name of the spirit who conceals illnesses is Kiu-ping-ping-lo (1), A-chi-na-chi-ping-ping-lo (2), U-hu-ta-ping-ping-lo (3), A-chi-na-chi-ping-ping-lo (4), Svāhā. [Use] one *jin* of mugwort and one *dou* of water.
Boil [the ingredients] until three *sheng* remain; recite the mantra over them three times.
Have the patient sit facing east and administer one *sheng* per day for three days.
The name of the yellow-disease demon is: (1) Hudu-lu-ye-ā-zhī-ná-zhī-chī-pō; (2) Ā-ná-qí-chī-pō; (3) Hú-li-tuó-chī-ná-tuó-chī-pō; (4) Yí-qí-ná-zhī-chī-pō; (5) Svāhā; (6) Thirty-seven fingernails.
Take two taels of apricot kernels and one *dou* of water;
boil until three *sheng* remain, and recite the mantra seven times over it.
Take one sheng daily;
place one cord in each eye and two cords in each nostril,
and consume the remainder as a potion.
After taking this three times a day,
take yellow and white thread and, having recited the mantra over it,
tie seven knots. First bind the head, then the two ears, then the neck, and finally the two elbows.
Subsequently, bind the hands and recite the mantra seven times.

The names of the demons who consume human marrow, as well as heart and liver, are: 1. Mukhadevi; 2. Aṭaṇajñi; 3. Aryagijñi; 4. Aśramajñi; 5. Anutajñi; 6. Arvanatijñi; 7. Atanijñi; 8. Ahūhūhūhūhūjñi; 9. Aphuphuphuphuji; Svāhā. Mix thirteen *hu* of hot water with one *sheng* of white powder.
Chant the mantra three times over one cup of water for a ritual bath and drink it.
For daily use, employ one hu and five dou;
it is auspicious to first pour it over the head.

If one suddenly encounters a whirlwind or suffers from dizziness and vertigo, recite this mantra named "Beautiful Sound" (*Svaraghoṣā*) twenty-one times over water and sprinkle it three times: 1. *tadā-hū-jina* 2. *no no no-hū-jina* 3. *arjā-ar-hū-jina* 4. *svāhā* Sprinkle [the water] three times.
The names of the wine-addicted spirits are: 1. Aratūna-aha, 2. Unāha, 3. Hurulda, 4. Hurulda, 5. Jyotika-jyotika, 6. Śamaka-śamaka. Svāhā! On the fourteenth or fifteenth day.
Take water from seven wells and three grains of salt.
Recite the mantra over them three times and pour the water over the crown of the head three times.
Spit into the ears three times and into the nose three times; drink the remaining water.
This person sits facing north.

The names of the *piśācas* who do not relish food are: 1. Antahū; 2. Phana-phe phana-phe antahū; 3. Uhū-hū hū-hū antahū; 4. Prāsidu-ya antahū; 5. Cāṇakhi antahū; 6. Aññāṇi antahū; 7. Svāhā. The thread is two colors: white and black.
Perform fourteen knots with a mantra.
Recite the mantra seven times over water and give it to the messenger to drink.

[The symptoms are] eating little but vomiting much. The names of the spirits are: 1. Citāhu; 2. Ajñātaka; 3. Varākiṇa; 4. Hāsanakiṇa; 5. Ajñānakina; 6. Aghakiṇa. [Recite] "Ajñānakina Aghakiṇa Svāhā. Recite the mantra seven times over water, sprinkle it on the face three times, and drink the remainder.
Having prepared a hemp rope, one should regularly use it at dawn to bind the patient's neck,
causing the patient to sit facing east.
[This shall be effective] for one day without fail, up to seven days.

The deafening spirits are named: (1) Hulu-dou, (2) Hou-hou-hou-hou Hulu-dou, (3) A-he-he-na Hulu, (4) A-ruo-ruo-ruo Hulu-dou, (5) A-ta-ta Hulu-dou, (6) Svāhā. [Take] three *sheng* of small beans and one *dou* of water.
When boiled down to three *shēng*,
add half a *shēng* of honey and clarified butter;
boil until it reaches two *shēng*.
Recite the mantra seventy times over clean water.
At dawn, place beans upon cotton with a compassionate mind;
take them up seven times while reciting the name of the spirit twice.

The mantra for the *kṣepaka* spirit named *Pūpūlodu*: (1) *Aṭanici pūpūlodu*, (2) *Hū hū hū hū ya pūpūlodu*, (3) *Sumate pūpūlodu*, (4) *Hu hu aṭana pūpūlodu*, (5) *Svāhā*. Recite this three times over water and spit it onto the face of the patient.
Cīdunā (1), Pūripūricīdunā (2), A-ha-ha-na (3), Huliduci-cīdunā (4), Huhu-hu-arya-cīnā (5), Svāhā (6). The patient should sit facing east.
Recite the mantra three times over a jar of water and seven willow twigs;
place them upon the jar in the east, south, west, and north.
Once the recitation is complete, sprinkle these four directions with the water.
Turn the face three times and drink it three times.

For the ghosts, there are twenty-five kinds: (1) *Phreṭa*, (2) *Phrapra phrapra phreṭa*, (3) *Uhu huṭa phreṭa*, (4) *Ahou houhou phreṭa*, (5) *Acīcī cīcī phreṭa*, (6) *Kareṭa jihuna phreṭa*, (7) *Svāhā*. Recite this mantra over water seven times and spit upon it.
Tie seven knots with thread of five colors and fasten them around the neck.
[Recite] "A-nā-gi (1), Chang-chang-nang A-nā-gi (2), Li-ti-nang A-nā-gi (3), A-jo-ti-na A-nā-gi (4), Svāhā (5). Recite this mantra over water twenty-eight times.
Spit upon the five sense organs and spit upon the ulcer, washing them three times.
Recite the mantra seven times over water: "Kṣīla, ghost-name Māpe (1), dhāraṇate māpe (2), śaryadhā māpe (3), abhīta ānāpe (4), svāhā (5)."
Spit upon the five sense organs as if washing a sore.

[Recite] the names of the toad-poisoning spirits: 1. *Pakṣaṇī*, 2. *Uhu-ludhu-sapakṣaṇī*, 3. *Yapadhu-pakṣaṇī*, 4. *Aryajñi-pakṣaṇī*, 5. *Svāhā*. Recite this mantra over water three times and spit it upon the five sense organs while also washing the sore.
It is auspicious to drink the remaining water.

The names of the hearth-demons are: 1. Prakīrṇaka-prakīrṇaka-dhūpa-kīrṇaka; 2. Cakra-dhūpa-kīrṇaka; 3. Amāgati-dhūpa-kīrṇaka; 4. Āhuli-dhūpa-kīrṇaka; 5. Svāhā. [Take] three dou of water and one handful of white powder.
Recite this seven times over water, then sip three mouthfuls.
Use the remainder to wash the ulcer for up to three days.

To exorcise the old ghosts, recite the following names: (1) Hou-hou, (2) Nu-tuo-nu-hou-hou, (3) Ni-duo-na-hou-hou, (4) A-ruo-dou-hou-hou, (5) A-ta-nu-hou-hou, (6) Bi-lü-duo-hou-hou, (7) Nu-ta-nu-hou-hou, (8) Svāhā. Take three dou of water in a copper basin and cover it with a white silk cloth.
Place seven pieces of willow branch upon it,
both lengthwise and crosswise,
and recite the mantra twenty-one times.
When finished, discard it in the latrine.
[The mantra for] the ghost named *Cchattani-paurāṭi*: *Cchattani* (1), *Aryaṭi* (2), *Cchattani* (3), *Muryaṭi* (4), *Amuryaṭi* (5), *Svāhā* (6). Use three bundles of white leeks.
Bind five cun of thread together.
Take one dou of Sichuan pepper and two dou of water;
boil until one dou remains.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times.
Take one *sheng* of it and drink it;
use the remainder to wash the ulcer.
The red-eyed ghost is named: (1) Onuta-aryatuntha, (2) Onuta-muladeina, (3) Onuta-yajñuntha, (4) Onuta-carmadeina, (5) Svāhā. Take three sheng of yeast and one dou of water.
Having boiled it down to three sheng,
take two sheng and recite the mantra twenty-one times.
Take one *śāṇa* of [the aforementioned substance] each day and apply it with saliva;
likewise wash the eyes for twenty-one days.

The nasal tumors caused by the *yakṣas* named Cāpala (1), Ajitacāpala (2), Pūrṇatāni-cāpala (3), Pūrvātāni-cāpala (4), Ajitātāni-cāpala (5), and Parvatātāni-cāpala (6)—[for these, recite] Svāhā (7). Take one *dōnī* of bitter wine and three *dōnī* of water.
Fry [the ingredients] until two *sheng* are obtained and recite the mantra twenty-one times.
Use two *zhu* daily for nasal irrigation for thirty-one days.

The name of the yakṣa who causes axillary odor is: (1) Juedanuzhi, (2) Houhouhouhoutanuzhi, (3) Fuliuliuliutanuzhi, (4) Molaiditanuzhi, (5) Ananantanatanuzhi, Svāhā. [Use] three *sheng* of lime and three *sheng* of bitter wine.
Chant the mantra thirty-seven times over a plate and place it [upon the patient].
For a man, first place it under the left armpit; for a woman, first place it under the right armpit.

This is the water-swell-demon named Huludouning, as spoken by the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka: (1) *bīruti*, (2) *huludouning*, (3) *āhū hū hū hū huludouning*, (4) *ruhu huludouning*, (5) *pazhuning*, (6) *huludouning*, *svāhā*. Use three *shu* of water and three *dou* of salt.
Fry it until one hu and five dou are obtained.
Recite the mantra thirty-five times.
Seal it with the name of the spirit and consume one dou daily.

The names of the *piśāca* demons are: (1) Pācilu, (2) Anidhuluta-pācilu, (3) Yenu-pācilu, (4) Anulitaṇu-pācilu, (5) Añjalitaṇu-pācilu, (6) Svāhā. Using eight *dǔ* of water, one *shèng* of small beans, and salt, recite the mantra twenty-one times.
Five *dou* were boiled down.
On clear days, he took two portions;
the remaining thick residue was made into cakes the size of a palm.
Apply this to the upward-facing classes [of spirits].

The names of the blind and sightless *kumbhāṇḍa* ghosts are: (1) Kau-ban-te’a A-jo-t’ou; (2) A-pu-li-ti A-jo-t’ou; (3) Chi-mi-ti A-jo-t’ou; (4) Mo-lai-ti A-jo-t’ou; (5) A-lo-ti A-jo-t’ou; (6) Man-chi-ti A-jo-t’ou; (7) Svāhā. Use ground black pepper, *aśmantaka* seeds, fine root (*su-sin*), *ren-shen* (ginseng), ginger, small red beans, and hemp seeds.
Take one *zhu* of each [ingredient] and grind them into a powder; mix it with honey syrup or grape syrup.
Recite the mantra seven times daily for up to seven days.
Then, fashion cakes the size of a coin.
Use this to apply over the eyes, then sprinkle water from the back of the head.
For the scabies-demons named: (1) *Huyou-yipodi*, (2) *Nahuyou-erji-moti*, (3) *Nahuyou-san-shoulüdi*, and (4) *Nahuyou-sishahe*—take one *hu* of water and add five *dou* of salt.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times and boil it seven times for use in bathing.

For the wall-crawling ghost named Houmouloudi (Hūmūruti): 1. Vima-ta-houmouloudi; 2. A-ruo-douni-houmouloudi; 3. Fuli-duo-ni-houmouloudi; 4. Svāhā. Use three *shu* of water and three *dou* of mugwort.
Boil [the ingredients] seven times while reciting the mantra twenty-one times.
Sprinkle it upon the four walls and the interior of the house.

1. *Mūṣikā-nāmānarthaka kvaṅ kvaṅ kvaṅ anarthaka svāhā* (2) 2. *Devī-anarthaka anarthaka svāhā* (3) 3. *Rakṣa rakṣa rakṣa rakṣa anarthaka svāhā* (4) 4. *Go go go go anarthaka svāhā* (5) 5. *Bubhukṣita bubhukṣita bubhukṣita bubhukṣita anarthaka svāhā* (6) 6. *Svāhā* (7) Recite the mantra over the ashes seven times.
Recite the mantra seven times over water and pour it into the hole;

continue this for up to three days. The names of the dog-spirits are: (1) Ciduti, (2) Visacini, (3) Kucuhuni, (4) Namijya, (5) Ucchahuni, (6) Svāhā. The names of the jaundice-demons are: (1) Yamudu, (2) Pabubodu, (3) Kicimi, (4) Yamusa, (5) Aphodidu, (6) Svāhā. [Then use] three pecks of water infused with saffron.
Recite the mantra seven times and drink it.
The names of the red-swelling spirits are: (1) Adūya, (2) Sukuḍādūya, (3) Yamabhyadūya, (4) Jāpamādūya, (5) Kautanvadūya, (6) Svāhā. Then take a square inch of red woolen cloth.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times and apply it to the red area.

For white swellings, the names of the ghosts are: (1) *Gimibi*, (2) *Pāradeti*, (3) *Gimuhi*, (4) *Gimibi*, (5) *Ukhyo-gimibi*, (6) *Husadū-gimibi*, *Svāhā*. Take one *dō* of water and as much white powder as half a chicken egg.
Recite this mantra twenty-one times, continuing for up to seven days.

The names of the ghosts who cause carbuncles are: (1) *Bidi-eka-he*, (2) *Biyou-bidi-er-he-mi-gi-mou*, (3) *Bidi-suo-hu-qiu*, (4) *Bidi-jugi-he-mi*, (5) *Svāhā*. By reciting this mantra, the ghost-arrows [shall be neutralized].
Recite this mantra twenty-one times for three days.

The mantra for the tooth-hiding demon named Huśudu is: (1) *huśudu*, (2) *ukhūna huśudu*, (3) *yamibī huśudu*, (4) *svāhā*. Take water from a well-blossomed lotus flower and recite this mantra over it seven times.
"Three times *haṃ*.
Regarding "the ground that has been for a long time":
one should apply powdered incense to the ground and sprinkle water upon it.
Once finished, smear it with stone incense.

The Cat-Demon (Māo-gui) employs various paths of suppression and sorcery, blending poisons with the Dong-bi-yen-mou-ding-su-an-ri-ghost; [the practitioner] touches the Lou-bi-shou-xu-qian-dou seal to shift and replace the ghost.
Yin yu wei bao jing du fu shu he bi ji zhou shui she mi bu wu zha you qi mu di | She po ta | Saha. Recite this mantra over water three times and sprinkle it; it will bring good fortune.
Bimbisāru-kumbhāṇḍa-rāja-huradurade (1) Usudāsaphuṣu (2) Kugīha-kuṭanajiphuṣu (3) Svāhā (4). This mantra has the power to command the Kumbhāṇḍa King and his host of soldiers.
It shatters [the body] like fine dust.
For all those who suddenly suffer from fever, thirst, heart pain,
as well as headaches and burning pains in the hands and feet;
Upon hearing this mantra, one immediately attains coolness.
Having recited the mantra over water three times, sprinkle it upon the afflicted area. Vaiśravaṇa.
His father's name was Pāṇḍara;
his mother's name was Supratiṣṭhitā;
his paternal uncle's name was Nanda.
The mother’s name was Makhilū; her father was the Heavenly King Pukkhala.
The mother’s name was Ukkācī; [her father was] Virūḷhaka.
His father’s name was Viśākha;
his mother’s name was Hārītī, the Mother of Demons;
his husband’s name was Piṅgala.
The eldest son of the Mother of Ghosts is named Vaiśravaṇa;
the middle one is named the General Saṃjñeya.
The younger son was named Maṇibhadra;
the eldest son was named Jyeṣṭhabhadra;
and the daughter was named Guṇavatī.
The names of the goiter-demons are: 1. Cāpamīcūparantaka, 2. Cāpamīcūparantaka, 3. Ujjūcāpamīcūparantaka. Svāhā! One should provide black honey syrup.
Recite the mantra seven times and twice more;
with each inhalation, snap your fingers once.

The name of the pus-licking ghost is Āpukuli (1) Kuli (2) Svāhā (3). The name of the Hu-pi ghost is Āpuccha (1) Amī Āpuccha (2) Amī Āpuccha (3) Amī Āpuccha (4) Svāhā (5). I am the Mother of Ghosts, whose name is Nami-bi.
I shall now proclaim a divine mantra to protect sentient beings,
to eliminate their false views and cause them to attain right view,
and to provide offerings of delicacies without depleting one's household wealth.
These worldly demons and ghosts are not as good as sacrificing to a dog for the sake of protection;
I shall now explain the correct truth for you.
Simply by using flowers, incense, ghee, milk, and gruel,

The seven celestial maidens bestowed upon me an efficacious medicine: when spat upon a mountain, the mountain collapsed; when spat upon a rock, the rock split asunder;
when spat upon water, the water was cut off; when spat upon fire, the fire was extinguished;
when spat upon gold, the gold was pierced; and when spat upon wood, the wood was broken.
The carbuncle of saliva dies with the saliva; the swelling of saliva is extinguished with the swelling.
A great fish in the ocean transforms into a frog.
When thunder arises from the southwest, its sound is not heard.
A frog dwells within it, devouring the moon.

with one spittle, it causes a thousand swellings and dies.
Spitting once upon a single boil causes a thousand boils to cease.
May my incantation be fulfilled according to my wish.
Thus have I heard the *Maṇirohaṇa-dhāraṇī-sūtra* spoken by the Buddha.
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park,
together with a great community of bhikṣus.
The Buddha spoke the Maṇibhadra Sūtra.
The Buddha asked Ānanda:
"For what reason do the people of the world fail to attain peace and security?
"Because the myriad people of the world are afflicted by many illnesses."
For what purpose are these used for illness? The pain of giving birth is used for abdominal pain;
the pain of death is used for heart pain; and the pain of a headache is used for headaches.
Dizziness and the inability to eat or drink are all the work of Māra.
Now, O bhikṣus.
Terrified in this way,
he then stepped forward and said to the Buddha,
"From where does this pain come?"
"Where has he gone?
The people are filled with great sorrow.
The Buddha then assembled the bhikṣus: Mahākāśyapa, Aniruddha, Revata, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Śāriputra, Ānanda, and Indira.
In the *Buddhabhāṣita-maṇiratna-sūtra*, the Buddha then enumerates the names of the seven Buddhas:

first, Vipaśyin Buddha; second, Śikhin Buddha; third, Viśvabhū Buddha; fourth, Krakucchanda Buddha; fifth, Kanakamuni Buddha; sixth, Kāśyapa Buddha; and seventh, Śākyamuni Buddha. He further declares that this present sutra has emerged from the mouths of all these Buddhas.

The first is Śikṣāra; the second, Gandhāra; the third, Lūtāra; the fourth, Mikhalā; the fifth, Kambuśīra; the sixth, Tailāra; the seventh, Asura; the eighth, Sūśramaṇa; the ninth, Susuṇḍa; and the tenth, Mandikejatu. [These include] all people, both great and small.
For those who have contracted diseases or are beset by suffering and calamity,
the Buddha now commands that all bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
and upāsikās shall recite this from memory.
There are ghosts of countries, ghosts of mountains;
ghosts of forests, ghosts of plants and trees;
ghosts of tombs, and ghosts from among burial mounds.
There are ghosts of the earth, ghosts of the heavens,
ghosts of the Big Dipper, ghosts of the void,
ghosts of marketplaces and wells, and ghosts of the dead.
There are ghosts of living beings and ghosts of the hungry.
There are ghosts within the path and ghosts outside the path; ghosts within the hall and ghosts outside the hall.
There are ghosts within water and ghosts on the edge of water; ghosts within fire and ghosts on the edge of fire.
There are ghosts within the body and ghosts outside the body;
there are ghosts of food and drink and ghosts of the time of sleep.
Now the Buddha says that there are red ghosts and black ghosts.
There are long ghosts and short ghosts;
there are tall and large ghosts and low and small ghosts;
there are medium-sized ghosts and white-colored ghosts.
There are yellow ghosts, there are blue ghosts;
there are black ghosts, there are ghosts of dreams;
and there are ghosts of childbirth.
The Buddha said: "If there should arise swords or staves born of anger and hatred, one should in all cases recite this Maṇiratna Sūtra;
then all the ghosts and spirits will spontaneously shatter."
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"If there are those who receive and uphold this sutra,
or those who are sick and emaciated..."
One should always recite this sutra.
If one suffers from headaches, blurred vision, chills and fevers,
or heart ailments, one should constantly read this Maṇiratna Sūtra.
All ghosts and spirits will then be spontaneously shattered.
Should there arise officials of the state, thieves, robbers, water,
or fire, one should immediately recite this Maṇiratna Sūtra.
The various ghosts and spirits shall no longer be able to harass or harm people.
Now, within this sutra produced from the Buddha’s own mouth, there are two classes of ghosts in the land:
the first is named Shen-sha, and the second is named Fu-qiu.
These two demons are fierce in their pursuit of people's vulnerabilities.
If one suffers from headaches, dizziness, heart pain, chills, or fever,
one should then recite the names of these two spirits.
