Trimaṇḍa papphāva pārima mahā.
"Anāśaha.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the great assembly, saying:
"In the past, throughout incalculable kalpas..."
When he was still an ordinary person (pṛthagjana), his name was Jātadhara.
In the kingdom of Kālañjara, he served as a merchant;
his business of buying and selling was deceptive and devoid of reality.
The various evil deeds he committed were beyond measure;
his lewdness and lack of moral conduct cannot be fully described.
At that time, out of folly, he harmed his father and doted on his mother for many years.
All the people of the nation know this;
they cry out in unison, saying, "This is Śatānīka!
He has killed his father and loved his mother for many years now."
At that time, I reflected that I was no different from the six domestic animals and possessed no human qualities.
Then, in the kingdom of Kālaṅgara,
I leaped over the city wall at night and fled toward a deep forest.
At that time, the king of this country was named Viśāla.
He issued a proclamation to the people of the realm, saying:
"This Caṇḍāla is a lecherous, profligate, and unprincipled man who has brought about this matter."
"To whoever is able to capture this man,
I shall grant a generous reward of precious goods.
At that time, the people of this country each accepted the recruitment and desired to seize my person.
At that time, struck with terror, he immediately left his country to become a śramaṇa.
In another land, he practiced the ten wholesome paths of action;
sitting in meditation and studying the Way, he wept day and night.
After thirty-seven years had passed,
because of the hindrance of the five heinous crimes,
his mind could not attain concentration, and he was overwhelmed by grief and sorrow beyond measure.
For thirty-seven years, while dwelling in a mountain cave, he constantly raised his voice in lamentation, crying out, "Alas!
Alas! By what means shall I depart from this suffering?"
In his grief, he went down into a cave to beg for food.
On the path, he found a large alms bowl containing a single casket of scriptures; there were no other scriptures within it.
There is only the *dhāraṇī* for the Joy of Accumulating Dharmas and the Abandonment of Suffering.
It is said that when the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges were about to enter *nirvāṇa* in the past,
they always resided in the kingdom of Vaiśālī.
This dhāraṇī was spoken and entrusted to the great bodhisattvas.
Should anyone in the future hear this dhāraṇī, that person,
in their past lives, [must have...]
One should cause them to hear of the practice of the five precepts and the ten wholesome actions; yet there are those who,
though they hear of them, do not take them to heart.
Those who do not practice it are said to be without a focal object.
This dhāraṇī can eliminate the great sins of the five heinous acts and the cycle of birth and death for ten billion kalpas.
If there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite it, [they shall be liberated].
One shall never fall into the three miserable realms of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, or animals.
Why is this? Because all Buddhas of the past, when they were about to enter parinirvāṇa, specifically instructed that this should be taught.
They shall honor, praise, and revere him, extolling his immeasurable merit.
To all bodhisattvas and future sentient beings who hear this dhāraṇī, [he shall entrust it].
The merit resulting from practicing with a mind of attachment is incalculable,
like the ocean of jewels on Mount Sumeru;
ordinary beings are unable to measure it.
If there are those who commit various evil deeds and merely hear the name of this dhāraṇī without practicing it,
yet harbor it once within their hearts, they shall fall into hell.
Within all the hells, the suffering and pain shall cease through the grace of this person. There are those who,
being able to practice with diligence in their present bodies,
attain realization through cultivation and behold hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddha-fields.
The merit obtained is immeasurable and cannot be fully described;
only the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas can exhaustively fathom it,
while those of the two vehicles, the Śrāvakas, cannot know it.
Why is this? This dhāraṇī was not spoken by one Buddha or two Buddhas;
it was spoken by all the Buddhas of the past, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
At that time, having obtained this sutra,
I immediately ceased begging for food;
filled with joy, I went toward the cave and entered within it.
He burned incense, prostrated, and praised him with tears of compassion;
he practiced and recited the sutras within the cave for one year,
but was only then able [to proceed] because of his karmic obstacles.
He was unable to enter my heart.
At that time, during the night of an autumn moon,
I bathed and practiced for seven days.
Just as there were many instances of confusion when the boy first began his training,
he practiced for another seven days,
yet it was no different; he remained just as confused as before.
With a mind filled with sorrow and distress, not knowing what to do,
he contemplated the written characters of this dhāraṇī within his thoughts;
after several repetitions, his mind suddenly became settled.
At that time, I was filled with joy,
like a person who finds a hundred thousand catties of gold in the earth;
though no one else knows of it, his inner delight does not cease.
I was likewise at that time;
after practicing for several years, my flight became unimpeded,
and I beheld the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
In the future, there will be practitioners who perform this according to the Dharma.

Avalokiteśvara speaks this *Svamanoratha-dhāraṇī*: *Namo Avalokiteśvarāya Bodhisattvāya*. *Tadyathā*: *Khara-pada khara-pada gaha-pada gha-pada ghana-pada svāhā*. One should practice this *dhāraṇī* method.
One should diligently perform prostrations and circumambulations in a quiet place,
reciting this dhāraṇī twelve thousand times;
one shall then behold Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
All one's wishes shall be fulfilled according to one's desire. To know good or bad fortune immediately upon requesting a dream, recite this *dhāraṇī*:

*Namō sarvabuddhānāṃ namō dharmāya namō saṃghāya* (Namo to the Triple Gem). *Namo maṇibhadra mahāyakṣasenāpate* (Homage to Maṇibhadra, the Great General of the Yakṣas). *Mahādaṇḍa dhāraṇī* (The *Dhāraṇī* of the Great Staff). *Nirīti-nirbhaya-gale hali-bhagale hūṃ* (O you who are free from suffering and fear, O you who possess the power of the world, hūṃ). *Aparājita aparājita* (Unconquered, unconquered). *Maṇibhadra-vana* (The Forest of Maṇibhadra). *Mahāgaṇḍa* (The Great Mass). *Pragaṇḍa* (The Foremost Mass). *Utpala-dhūpa-puṣpa-vikiraṇa* (Scattering blue lotuses, incense, and flowers).
Recite this one hundred and eight times before the Buddha;
then go to sleep and do not speak with anyone else.
Whatever you wish to accomplish will manifest within your dreams.
The *Dhāraṇī for Eliminating All Insanity and Madness*:

*namo lecane liśe liśe namo ’ridhe varuṭṭi śe varaliśe bodhisattve mahāsattve tathāgate jileme jile lekha lekha mahāliśe varuṭṭi śe varaliśe svāhā*. This mantra can eliminate all cases of insanity and madness.
One should tie a thread around the person's neck.
Whether it be a thread of five colors,
or if five colors are unavailable, one should use a red thread and recite this mantra over it three times.
Tying threads into three knots will immediately cure all forms of insanity.

This *dhāraṇī* for removing fear: *Namo buddhāya*. *Namo dharmāya*. *Namo saṃghāya*. *Namo ’rhitā*. *Namo lukkhiḍi*. *Śāvarāya*. *Bodhisattvāya*. *Mahāsattvāya*. *Tadyathā*: *Hārikā bhiriga*. *Karabing karāṭa*. *Śāśamukki*. *Sāṭandu*. *Sautuṣanaye*. *Sāṭandu*. *Uhasami*. *Muhusami*. *Japasami*. *Tambha*. *Svāhā*. If there are sons or daughters of good family...
Those who read and recite this dhāraṇī shall be freed from all fears,
including those arising from water, fire, thieves, and all malevolent spirits.
It can completely ward off all manner of terrors from tigers, wolves,
venomous beasts, and the like.
If one encounters bandits on the road, [it shall protect them].
Take a handful of earth and recite this dhāraṇī over it seven times.
Sprinkle it toward the thieves;
it will cause them to be repelled, making their eyes unable to see one another, so that they depart by way of the road.

The Dharani for Tying the Medicine Boundary: *Tadyathā | śūme | śūmavati | vāruṣi | varuṇe | mamale | hamale | mate | karame | svāhā*. One should take a thread prepared by a girl who maintains this mantra, recite it twenty-one times, and tie twenty-one knots.
Bind it to the finger.
Once the khaṭvāṅga-stake has been driven into the ground,
this is called the medicinal formula for binding.
After forming the intention regarding the Dharma, one then excavates the body.
There will then appear various forms and images;
if one obtains the image of an elephant, [it is so].
As it passed by with its food wedged in its throat,
lions, tigers, wolves, and other such predatory beasts fled in all directions upon seeing it,
not daring to approach or encircle it.
If one eats it, one will be able to see nāgas;
if one engages in sexual union with a woman, one's vigor will not be exhausted even after a hundred or a thousand times.
If one obtains the image of a horse, one should grind it and eat it.
If one drinks it when it is mixed [with water],
one will immediately attain *luti*.
For seven days, one can travel through the air for more than two thousand *li* without the *dhyāna-water* submerging.
If one obtains the form of a cow,
its strength when eating will equal that of ten elephants,
and it will live for two hundred years; of this there is no doubt.
If one obtains an image of a woman, one should carry it while traveling;
thus, one will attain mastery over all lands and perform more than a hundred meditative concentrations in a single day.
Their feet shall not grow weary;
wherever they go, they will be beloved by others;
and their speech shall be as exquisite and sweet as nectar.
Whoever hears this shall rejoice, believe, and accept it.
One will be pleasing to behold and take delight in attending to the affairs of others.
If one obtains a male image, one should always carry it with them.
If one drinks it at all times, one will attain a lifespan of two hundred years;
one's physical strength will be peerless, and none shall be able to overcome them.
He was handsome, intelligent, and possessed a majestic radiance;
if he fathered children, they too would resemble him.
All signs of old age were extinguished, and he returned to youthfulness.
He fully understands all worldly affairs.
Having heard one hundred thousand verses along with their meanings, he is able to retain them.
His physical eye is pure and clearly perceives even a *niti* (a mote of dust).
One who is brave, robust, and possesses great strength,
if they obtain the image of a ram and eat it,
will not suffer from hunger for thirteen months.
He delights in practicing martial arts and is invincible in battle;
his temperament is gentle and kind, and his body is stout.
If he obtains the image of a peacock, he immediately eats it himself.
Once all poisons have become incapable of causing harm,
one perceives more than a hundred meditative objects (*dhyāna-vastu*).
If one obtains the image of a snake, one may carry it while walking.
No one among all worldly people is able to do so.
If one uses it to smear upon the body,
one will attain great power and be able to fight with the Naga Andhaka without being harmed by his venom.
If one is bitten by a venomous creature or consumes a potent poison,
applying this to the body will ensure that no suffering arises.
If it is applied to the eyes, one will be able to see even a *niti* (a tiny insect).
If one obtains the image of a deer, one should carry it and practice with it;
no one among all worldly people will be able to do anything [to harm] them.
If one obtains the image of a deer entwined with the image of a snake, [the same applies].
Furthermore, it is said that if one eats the image of a tortoise, one's body will become as hard as stone;
if used to smear the body, the body cannot be destroyed,
such that even a vajra cannot harm it.
Even when struck by asuras, it cannot be destroyed;
it has no excrement or urine.
If one catches a frog, one may carry it while traveling.
They do not sink upon the water;
even when entering beneath the water, they suffer no harm.
They are always made joyful, such that none can surpass them.
If one obtains a conch shell shaped like an auspicious fruit and carries it while traveling,
people of the world will see its majestic radiance as being like that of the sun;
when the king hears of his arrival, he will come out a hundred paces to welcome him.
If the king desires to perform any undertaking in his mind, he shall enjoy its full fruition;
whatever he intends to do, it shall all be accomplished for him,
and every wish he conceives shall be granted to him in its entirety.
Furthermore, there is the Dream-Seeking Dhāraṇī: *tadyathā* | hārī hārī | mukhani trimukhani | svāhā. This is the dream-seeking mantra; recite it seven times when going to sleep.
If one sees nothing [in dreams], then by the end of the first seven days, one will certainly see something.

When the Buddha spoke this incantation, he said: "Namo Buddha; Namo Dharma; Namo Bhikṣusaṃgha; Namo to the Seven Buddhas of the Past; Namo to all Buddhas of the Present; Namo to all Buddhas; Namo to all disciples of the Buddhas. Having paid these respects, he then recited this incantation.

May it be fulfilled according to my wish: Akhani nikhani akhana nikhani abira mandari nikhani padani patiri. Homage to the Buddha! Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus! Homage to the Seven Buddhas of the Past! Homage to all the Buddhas of the Present! Homage to the disciples of all the Buddhas! Homage to all the Buddhas! Homage to the teachers and their disciples! May that which I now incantate be fulfilled according to my wish.

If a person suffers from seasonal epidemics or diseases, one should take a thread and recite the mantra over it seven times while writing the names of the malevolent spirits upon it. This should be tied to the end of the thread. When reciting the mantra, one must maintain purity through fasting and abstinence, rinse the mouth, burn incense, and speak with a focused and upright mind.
Whether walking or staying, according to whichever direction one turns for refuge, one should invoke the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions;
for instance, if a person walks toward the east and takes refuge in that Buddha, they should recite the name of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named *Dīpaṃkara*.
The same applies to the south, west, north, and the four intermediate directions.
When wishing to lie down, one should invoke the Buddha of the lower direction;
when rising, one should invoke the Buddha of the upper direction.
In the south is the Buddha named Prathamacittotpāda-bhayaviraja-ārambhana Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
In the west is the Buddha named Vajrapadavikrama Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
In the north is the Buddha named Ratnajñānaśirṣa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
In the northeast is the Buddha named Mānamadabhañjanapadavikrama-asaṃcaya Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
In the southeast, there is a Buddha named Adhicittonnata-avivartya-śirṣarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
In the southwest, there is a Buddha named Ratnacchattra-gaganāvabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
In the northwest, there is a Buddha named Kaishua (Vikāśin) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
In the nadir, there is a Buddha named Chufa-yi-nian-duan-yi-ba-yu (Prathamachittotpādavicikitsācchedakāmarāga) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
In the direction above is the Buddha named King Who Transcends Equality and Eliminates Darkness, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
I have compassion for all the dragon kings, both in the heavens and in the world;
by means of this compassionate mind of mine, may all poisons and hatreds be extinguished.
"By means of my mass of wisdom, I use the mind to slay this poisonous taste;
the poison is rendered tasteless. It is destroyed and enters the earth.
This verse was spoken by the Buddha.
If one recites this seven times every morning after having purified oneself, one will attain immeasurable merit, extinguish all evils, and be granted longevity.

The Buddha spoke this *Sarvamangalasarvapāpavināśana-dhāraṇī*: *Namo buddhāya | Namo dharmāya | Namaḥ saṃghāya | Namo śrībuddhasamaghataniprabhāvatāparakṣa-kūlipaṇḍa-maitrī-svargata-purīha-śeṣarā-tulokṣi-dhvanadī-tanmukhe.* This was spoken by the Buddha from within the chapter on "Contemplating the Four Dignified Postures" in the *Buddhānusmṛtisamādhi*. Furthermore, there is the transformation Buddha who instructs the various *śrāvakas*.
Counting the breaths through ānāpāna with flowing light;
visualizing white bones with flowing light from the white bones;
contemplating the mind as pure and contemplating the mind as impure.
The perception of the arising of fetters, the perception of the cessation of fetters;
the perception of the branches of severing fetters, and the perception of killing the roots of the fetters—
such perceptions are as numerous as the atoms in nine hundred billion worlds.
Such practices as counting the breath and *ānāpāna* are called the Dharma of the Śrāvakas.
As for the Dharma of the Bodhisattvas, there are only four methods:
first, to confess one's transgressions and repent at six periods throughout the day and night.
Second, they constantly practice mindfulness of the Buddha and do not deceive sentient beings.
Third, they cultivate the six points of harmonious respect and harbor no anger or pride.
Fourth, they practice the six recollections as if their heads were on fire.
The Buddha told the King, his father:
"Such names as these are called the Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddhas in Future Ages;
they are also called the Differentiation of the Buddha’s Body."
It is also called knowing the physical marks of the Buddha;
it is also called the Buddha-remembrance samādhi;
it is also called the radiance of all Buddhas.
Protecting and Sheltering Sentient Beings.
*Dhāraṇī-saṃgraha*, Volume Nine;
*Dhāraṇī-saṃgraha*, Volume Ten.
The author is unknown; these are now appended to the Liang Catalogue:
one *Dhāraṇī of Fixed Will and Wise Vision* in one fascicle, and one *Dhāraṇī of the Eight Brothers* in one fascicle.
One dhāraṇī for the manifestation of forms and the granting of wishes spoken by Avalokiteśvara;
one dhāraṇī for the elimination of sins and the vision of the Buddha from the *Sūryagarbha-sūtra*;
and one dhāraṇī for the deity Phala-labdha who increases virtue.
One dhāraṇī for the excellent protection that removes illness;
one dhāraṇī for advancing toward fruition, attaining realization, and cultivating practice;
and one dhāraṇī for removing drowsiness and receiving protection by tying a thread.
One dhāraṇī for removing drowsiness with clarified butter and alleviating hunger;
one dhāraṇī for beholding the Buddha and fulfilling vows;
and one dhāraṇī for Avalokiteśvara manifesting his body to bestow various vows and eliminate all illnesses.
One dhāraṇī for scattering flowers at the feet of Avalokiteśvara;
one dhāraṇī for reciting to Avalokiteśvara when seeking a boon;
and one dhāraṇī for removing all pain by reciting the mantra while rubbing the eyes with the hand.
One *dhāraṇī* for drinking salt water to cure abdominal pain;
one *dhāraṇī* for removing sudden poison and curing fatal illnesses;
and one *dhāraṇī* for removing anger. These are from the *Sūryagarbha-sūtra*.
One dhāraṇī for Avalokiteśvara for the removal of karmic obstructions, spoken by the Buddha;
one dhāraṇī for smearing the body, banners, medicinal ointments, poisons, and swellings with mud;
and one dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha who delights in emptiness.
One dhāraṇī for the repentance of Avalokiteśvara;
one dhāraṇī for casting flowers;
one dhāraṇī for cursing swellings.
One *dhāraṇī* for subduing malignant boils and sores;
one *dhāraṇī* for protecting the eyes from the *Sūryagarbha-sūtra*;
and the *Caturmahārāja-dhāraṇī* for removing all inauspiciousness—these comprise five *dhāraṇīs* in total. The *Samādhi-prajñā-darśana-dhāraṇī*. Homage to the Buddha. *Śeṣa*.
Namo dharmāya, namo saṃghāya dāmadāna.
Na-ja-na-ja-li-ja-na-pa-mei-ti (Najana-jari-janapame-ti)
Haraṇi haraṇi utpādapāśe svāhā. This dhāraṇī.
On the fifteenth day of the autumn moon, at the conclusion of the day,
one should enter the presence of an image of the Buddha *Cakṣuḥsaṃbhava* and surround it with yellow flowers.
Spread this over the ground for a length and breadth of one step.
When the white hour arrives in the east, recite it with a sincere mind one thousand times;
you will then be able to behold all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
This eradicates all karmic obstacles of birth and death.
Practice this for seven days.
Behind the image of the Buddha, paint a bodhisattva.
He is named the Bodhisattva Vajradhara.
One should also recite it one thousand times beforehand;
for one day, recite it before the image, and for the following day, recite it before the Bodhisattva.
If a person who practices this dhāraṇī should fall into the three miserable realms, such a thing is impossible.
If a person encounters illness or various evils approach them, [this dhāraṇī shall protect them].
Upon seeing [this], recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times.
The Dhāraṇī of the Eight Brothers: Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"There are eight brother-dhāraṇīs;
you should receive, uphold, read, recite, and expound them for others."
Abinū, Kubinū, Abari, Mucumudu, Pramudupramudu, Āmanu, Krumaṇu, Sīhuvita, Udrā, Udrā, Dibuda. The Buddha addressed Ānanda: [Thus it was said.]
These are the names of these eight brothers.
If there is anyone who knows the names of these eight brothers and hears this dhāraṇī, [they shall attain liberation].
If one upholds, recites, and keeps [this] in mind,
you should know that such a person cannot be harmed by poison, cannot be wounded by weapons,
cannot be burned by fire, and cannot be swept away by water.
All malevolent spirits, directional ghosts,
and enchanting demons; yakṣas, rākṣasas,
and all other evil spirits who are able to harm or terrify people.
Furthermore, all enmity, blame, strife, and litigation shall be entirely extinguished.
This was taught by the Buddhas of the past.

Avalokiteśvara has spoken this *dhāraṇī* for the manifestation of vows: *Namo Avalokiteśvarāya Bodhisattvāya | Taṃtitha | Kharañca | Kharañca | Gahañca | Gañca | Gañca | Svāhā*. This is the ritual method of this *dhāraṇī*.
One should diligently perform prostrations and circumambulate the stupa in a quiet place,
reciting this dhāraṇī twelve thousand times;
one shall then behold Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
All one's wishes shall be fulfilled according to one's desire.

In the *Sūryagarbha-sūtra*, regarding the *Pāpadeśanā-buddhadarśana-dhāraṇī*, Śākyamuni Buddha requested the Buddhas of the ten directions to dwell together in this Sahā world and simultaneously proclaim this dhāraṇī with a single voice.
Tatoṭhe, vītilambe vītilambe, upadāpiye vītilambe, śvapāle, anuttarātata anuttarātata, pudrakoṭi vītilambe, svāhā. The Buddha said: "If the disciples of the fourfold assembly..."
One who upholds, recites, and chants this dhāraṇī should bathe themselves in a pure place, put on fresh and clean garments,
and make offerings of excellent flowers and incense to the Buddha.
One should practice on the eighth day of the month.
After twenty-one days, one will eliminate the karmic offenses and calamities of past lives;
one will then attain face-to-face vision of the Buddhas of the ten directions, and after casting off this body, one will no longer undergo birth and death.
The meritorious deeds performed therein are unsurpassed;
now they are briefly explained. A practitioner shall not consume wine or meat.

They shall obtain the fruit and benefit of the *dhāraṇī* that increases goodness: *U-mu-ni*, *Pha-la-mu-ni*, *Kiu-po-men-he*, *Kiu-sse-pa-jung*, *A-po-lo-mu-sa-siang*, *Pi-t’a-lo-sse-ni-ti*, *Ka-to-ka-pa-li-li-pin-t’o-mo*, *Siang-sa-lo-chi-lo-mo-t’ui-lo-mo-u-yü-ti-ts’iu*, *A-nou-ti-ts’iu*, *Sa-po-so-mo-lu*, *Na-sha-na-siang*, *Pi-ti-she-mo-ts’iu*, *A-mei-lo-i*, *A-po-mie*, *Ch’iu-lo-ni-mie*, *Ni-ti-a*, *San-mu-li*, *Svāhā*. If there are good sons or good daughters...
One should receive, uphold, recite, read,
and transcribe these dharani phrases before a Buddha, an image, a stupa, or before the śarīra relics.
Recite it one thousand times.
By drinking black stone-melodious honey (*kṛṣṇa-śarkarā*) and lotus-stamen nectar,
one can recite it one thousand times in a single day and attain the knowledge of others' minds (*paracittajñāna*).
Good sons and good daughters, bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas and upāsikās,
who dwell in a quiet place and practice this dhāraṇī with sincerity according to the Dharma.
Within no more than seven days,
this person will attain the four dhyānas, destroy the fetters of the desire realm,
and realize the Samādhi of Seeing the Buddhas of the Ten Directions According to the Dharma-Intention.
It is able to transform sentient beings and extinguish all obstacles—
namely, the obstacle of karma and the obstacle of afflictions—
and it is able to purify all the faculties of sentient beings.
It can burn away all the fetters of sentient beings, such as afflictions and inversions;
it brings them close to dwelling in the path of the noble ones,
and can also cause them not to regress from bodhi.
One draws near to omniscience;
wisdom arises not from external causes,
and one attains the dharma-gate of the samādhi of unhindered fearlessness throughout the three periods of time for all Buddhas.

The Dhāraṇī for the Excellent Protection and Elimination of Disease: *tadyathā* | *varira* | *vicaṇavarira* | *vrajavaja* | *ajujubira khibnimā* | *khibnimahāha* | *munimunidhṛti* | *svāhā* | *sabinā* | *hohā arivaca-svāhā* | *svāhā*. If there is anyone who reads and recites this dhāraṇī, within a hundred *yojanas*, [there shall be no harm from] evil persons or non-human beings.
One cannot find an opportunity [to harm them].
Whether it be one's own illness or another's,
by reciting this, they shall be immediately cured.

The Dharani for Advancing to the Fruits, Attaining Realization, and Cultivating Practice: *Tathāgata-mūla-mūla-rā arghaṭa mūla-ra-vijaya svāhā*. If a person upholds, recites, and reads this, while also cultivating meritorious deeds, they shall enter the First Stage (*prathamā bhūmi*).
The *Dhāraṇī for Removing Drowsiness and Delusion by Tying a Thread*:
*Tadyathā parigale khuśule takale*.
Vasaṃgapagālidharacivara-pañcana.
Mukha-paroṇa-paroṇaṃ.
Pralam-akṣaya-sarpa-sarva-kṣayinī-caryā-bhūmi.
Līśe kilaṃna piśudha niṃ samalūpa pijjati.
Samantabhadra-dharma-nirghoṣa-vimala-śrī-cakra.

Ninandi-jī-asamparagi-nāma-riṇa Ninandi-jī-asamparagi-nāma-riṇa (Ninandi-jī-asamparagi-nāma-riṇa) is a mantra. It is also known as the *Ninandi-jī-asamparagi-nāma-riṇa* (The Mantra of Ninandi-jī Who Is Free from Fear). It is one of the mantras associated with the Vidyārājñīs (Queenly Knowledge-Holders) found in the *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-sūtra*. It is recited for the purpose of protection against various calamities, such as snake venom, poison, and other afflictions. (Note: The transliteration provided follows the standard Sanskrit phonetic system; however, variations in spelling may occur depending on the specific tradition or source text.)
Apariśatana tiṣyapuṣyānandhe.
This dhāraṇī, "Tatha bidata neng saha," is the method for removing drowsiness and maintaining the practice.
On the fourteenth day, before a true relic or a true image, or before a true stūpa,
using various incenses and flowers and two *zhang* of white cotton thread,
recite [the mantra] once for each knot; make eight hundred knots.
If one wishes not to sleep, one should tie it around one's neck;
this will entirely eliminate the desire for sleep.
When one wishes to sleep, one should place it in a clean spot beneath a ridge.
One should burn incense, make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise.
All devas and benevolent spirits will protect this person.

The *Dhāraṇī for Eliminating Sleep and Hunger while Benefiting with Milk*: *tuṭṭe nimme nimme nirmale heṣaṇḍe samuṇḍe vākce vikace pūṇe varicche samukhite samudane namo vākavate buddhasya siddhe mudrāpade tāradve bhṛtiśakte trapalambhe svāhā.* If a person suffers from excessive sleep, [they should recite this].
By reciting this dhāraṇī one thousand times and applying it to the eyes,
one will have no sleep; by applying it to the feet,
one can travel ten yojanas in a single day.
If one eats it, it will cause a person not to feel hunger.
If women, cattle, or sheep produce little milk, one should recite the mantra over water one thousand times and drink it; then their milk will become abundant.

The *Dhāraṇī of Seeing the Buddha According to One’s Wishes*: *tathā-tathā dhāraṇī dhāraṇī dhāriṇi mūṅgaparava-saṅgi siddhi cāndrili naihali lokapatti buddhapatti dilli ugratijñe rāśupagati tigipatti viśrabuddhe dharmaparivakṣasakepikape jūti amṛtakepe hūtasamim nidhasamahiti-tija-kilikabatti śūnabuddhe indriliśabuddhe svāhā*. If there are good sons or good daughters...
One who wishes to practice this dhāraṇī should bathe themselves to purify, don clean garments,
and make offerings of flowers, incense, and lamps to the Buddha.
From the eighth day of the month to the fifteenth,
recite the dhāraṇī during the six periods of the day and night,
reciting it one hundred and eight times for each period.
At that moment, one immediately beholds the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
seated upon a lotus throne and preaching the Dharma;
he then grants that person whatever they have wished for.
Whether seeking extensive learning, or seeking the knowledge of past lives;
whether seeking precious jewels, or seeking a pure buddha-field;
whether seeking a high position, or seeking mastery in the arts and crafts.
Whether seeking eloquence or seeking the removal of karmic obstructions,
all that such a person wishes for shall be granted.
This applies to one who practices the dhāraṇī.
One should practice this by fasting for three days.
It may not be performed during the second, third, or eighth months, nor at other times.
This *dhāraṇī* of Avalokiteśvara’s manifestation, which bestows various vows and eliminates all illnesses, is: *Siddhārthasamantabhadra namo buddhāya*.
Namo dharmāya, namo saṃghāya, namo āryāya.
Vairocanaprabhāśa-bodhisattvaḥ.
mahāsattva śrīkṛtapraparākrami buddhasamādhimabhiṣṭhāmi.
Sattvanamojñāpaya vilokaya mudrā.
Parāvasitanam u āliśa parugiti śivaraśa.
Bodhisattva, mahāsattva, mahā-kāruṇika.
Gāyana namo sarvabandhanachedanāya gāyana namo bhāṣābhāṣaṇāya.
Makara-sarpa sarvasattvanamitracitta-ugra-vibhīta-sarpa.
Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya. Tadyathā:
pāra-pāra-samudra-tīrtha-viśuddha-svabhāva-ākṣaye. Svāhā.
Sarvasattva-śokāpahantā-jīra-jīrāṇi.
Vārasa-ravi-sara-buddha-kṣetra-sarpa-buddha-kṣetra-sarpa.
Bodhisatva Bodhisatva Sarva-...
Sattva-bhūtānām kṣipra bodhi-satya bodhi-satya.
Bodhisatve Bodhisatve Maitri.
Āryaśabarītiśaparāśaḥ (or Āryaśabarītiśaparāśā)
Mala mala samāju sarvasattvanamitratācitta saṃvidhatsva mokṣa.
Kara ki li ki li
Jili jili jili
Jili jili jili
Ji li dou liu dou liu
Dhuru dhuru bodhi!
Bodhi bodhi sarpamṛte!
Cease the flow,
cease the flow;
let the flow be exquisite.
Xiu flows through the groves;
his carriage is there.
Ākṣepa sarvasattvabhūtānām ākṣepa sarvasattvānām.
Kāruṇikadhāraṇī śvāna-saṭṭha saṭṭha saṭṭha.
Bhṛtikā, Śrīmā,
and Vāraṇa.
Ṭaṇa ṭaṇa kaṇa kaṇa śūli śūli mahā.
Xiūliúmí shāhē nà mó ālíshe.
Varuṇadhiśa varāśe svadhāṃtuḥ.
Regarding this *muktāprabha svāhā* dhāraṇī, how should it be practiced?
One should use fine, white, clean cotton cloth or fine linen.
Paint an image of Avalokiteśvara.
He is clad in white robes and seated upon a lotus throne; in one hand he holds a lotus flower, and in the other he holds a *kamaṇḍalu*.
It causes one's hair to stand on end.
Those who wish to practice this should recite this dhāraṇī before an image of Avalokiteśvara.
When performing the rite, on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight,
one should put on new,
clean garments and smear the ground with pure cow dung.
Furthermore, one should smear fragrant mud upon it and generate a mind of reverence,
placing twelve vessels filled with fresh milk within it.
Use four earthenware vessels to hold fine fragrant liquid.
One requires sixteen jars of the finest fragrant flowers and sixteen earthenware lamps.
Burn solid black agarwood incense.
Take four large earthen jars and fill them with pure water;
place various kinds of flower branches within them.
One should burn soft wood fuel and also require eight hundred lotus flowers.
At that time, one should recite this dhāraṇī,
maintaining a continuous flow of sound and an uninterrupted state of virtuous mind.
Recite the mantra once and cast one flower into the fire.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva shall appear from the east, manifesting a great divine radiance.
When the fire was blazing fiercely,
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva appeared within the flames,
just like the painted image.
Clad in white garments with hair standing erect,
holding a flower in a vase, he appears within the fire;
upon seeing him, one’s mind shall be free from all fear.
It should be known that such a person closes the gates to the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals.
Whatever they desire or seek, they shall obtain it all—
whether seeking wealth and nobility, or seeking to fly through the air.
If they wish to bestow gifts upon sentient beings, they shall obtain complete mastery and fulfillment of their will.
Whether they seek extensive learning, seek to engage in debate,
enter the ocean to seek hidden treasures, partake in the elixir of the immortals, seek exquisite beauty, or aspire to be born in the heavens— [all shall be attained].
If one seeks the divine eye and divine ear, or wishes to extinguish all physical ailments—
whether the body’s faculties are incomplete,
or if one suffers from chronic illnesses, leprosy, or any other form of disease and suffering.
Even those whose bodies or sense faculties are incomplete shall all attain healing and recovery;
furthermore, all past heavy karmic obstacles shall be eliminated.
If a man desires a female body, [he shall obtain it].
If a woman desires to obtain a male body,
she shall attain it entirely according to her wish.
Once she has finished making her request as she desires, she should then send back Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.

The Dharani for Scattering Flowers at the Feet of Avalokiteśvara: Namaḥ sarvebhyaḥ | Namo ’ryebhyaḥ | Vairocanaprabhā | Tadyathā | Kiri | Ciri | Kiri | Ciri | Śūlu | Śūlu | Gaca | Gaca-sa-tu-ṣṭe | Arye | Vairocanaprabhā | Svāhā. One should take a handful of fine flowers.
Recite this dhāraṇī three times,
then scatter handfuls of flowers at the feet of Avalokiteśvara and offer fine incense as an offering.

The *Dhāraṇī for Recalling Avalokiteśvara to Fulfill Wishes*: *namo āryāya* | *varodgate śāvarāya* | *bodhisattvāya* | *mahāsattvāya* | *tadyathā* | *dhu dhu dhu* | *asamasamālini* | *tūrṇapramālini* | *tuttabhinamunama* | *svāhā*. For this mantra, one should burn aloeswood incense and recite it three times.
Recite this mantra with a sincere mind while mindful of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
This mantra is auspicious;
it can eliminate all past karmic offenses and bring about the attainment of great merit.
If you desire and pray for anything, it shall surely be obtained as wished.
By reciting this mantra and rubbing the eyes with the hand, all pain is removed.
*Dhāraṇī namo buddhāya namo dharmāya*.
Namo saṃghāya, namo lokeṣu,
namo āryebhyaḥ.
Vajrapāṇi bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Tataṭa khu khuvici cūlibi mi mṛle mṛli śudha ṇam.
Gacchati-milā-sarva-ukṣa-lokaśamaṇi-vināśani.
Cetāni vicetāni vata sumedha bhikkhu sumedha.
Dhanasiri-ma-samukhaṃ dhanasani-pāda-samukhaṃ dhanam.
Sarvasattvānāṃ śāntiḥ viśāntiḥ āryāḥ.
Varuṇadeva bodhisattva deśana.
Recite this mantra, *naṃ śāntiḥ svāhā*,
one hundred and eight times.
Rubbing it with one's own hand over the eyes can eliminate all ailments and pains of the visual faculty.

The *dhāraṇī* for eliminating abdominal pain: *Namo le naṃ liśe śe | namo āliśe | bharakṣite śabaraśe | bodhisattvaśe | mahāsattvaśe | tathāgata | jyotirjyotiḥ | jyotirañji | anasravataniye | svāhā*. Recite this mantra three times over salt water.
If one drinks this, it cures abdominal pain.

This *dhāraṇī* for removing sudden poison and curing fatal illnesses is as follows: *Namo lele, liśe, śe. Namo āliśe. Varuṭiśe, varāśe. Bodhisattvaśe, mahāsattvaśe. Tadyathā: sarisari, vilivili, sarvaviṣanāśani. Svāhā.* If a person is afflicted by poison and is on the verge of death, [recite this].
If [the patient] has already died,
recite this dhāraṇī into the ear of the sick person; by the power of the incantation,
they will immediately recover, and if they have died, they will return to life.
The Dhāraṇī for Eliminating Anger, from the Sūryagarbha:
Tadyathā: Puṣpaka buddhabuddhara.
Ilāra ilāvahe luha lūga gagana.
Cāmya māye rāme rāje cakrāvartte bhagavartte lute khe khele vaghe khe.
Vaha kṣi nara jaṭa śe ḍa na me ṭaṃ.
Cedi-mite pāli-miṭṭhe miṇḍe kheḷa-miṭṭhe miṭṭhe khagga-miṭṭhe.
Sambuja-mai-sasakāra-mai-maṇavada-mai.
*Bhadi ambara me svāhā*.

This dhāraṇī can eliminate all anger among worldly people. If one wishes to cause all people not to give rise to anger toward oneself, take *campaka* oil and recite this [dhāraṇī] over it seven times.
Having consecrated the hands and eyes with this mantra,
the wrathful minds of all humans, non-humans, māras, nāgas,
ghosts, and even animals shall be dispelled.
Suppose that all the humans, non-humans, devas, māras, nāgas,
and ghosts throughout the four continents were to give rise to intense hatred toward me;
one should take a handful of water at the clear dawn, recite the mantra over it seven times, and sprinkle it in the four directions.
If used for washing the face, the anger of all who are wrathful will immediately be dispelled.
Even if the waters of the great oceans in the four directions were all in turmoil,
sprinkling this [substance] would always cause them to become clear.
How much more so for human beings!

The Buddha spoke this *Dhāraṇī for the Elimination of Karmic Obstructions*: *Namo buddhāya* | *Namo dharmāya* | *Namo saṃghāya* | *Namo āryāya* | *Varuṇe tiṣyapālāya* | *bodhisattvāya* | *mahāsattvāya* | *tadyathā* | *jambavijaye* | *vidhubhime* | *merupriye* | *garudā* | *bhimekule* | *jambuki* | *saṃśibhime* | *bodhisattvakakaloma-kṣāya* | *bhime* | *svāhā*. This mantra can eliminate the sins of karmic obstructions from beginningless birth and death, since the time one first possessed consciousness and received a physical body.
If one recites this *Dhāraṇī Divine Mantra Sūtra* a thousand times on the fifteenth and thirtieth days of every month, one shall obtain immeasurable merit.
If one recites this once every morning as spoken by Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
all evils will be warded off. Namo Lennatolaye-saye.
Namo ārya-vairocana-svabhāva-śuddha-svabhāvebhyaḥ.
Bodhisattva mahāsattva tadyathā.
Kūṭi kūṭitāluḍaḥ.
Douduliepo duosimomi poluoheliduo.
Svāhā. Namo Ratnatrayāya. Namo Āryāya.
Vajrapāṇi bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Tataṭa cili mili cili lekha lekha mahāliśe.
Paroṭi śāvara sara bodhisattva mahāsattva buddhabhāṣitamantradhāraṇī tathāgata.
Ili phuli chiriphulenti ālai bhumalai bhuṃ.
Varivūṃ bhiḥ varivūṃ bhiḥ svasti bhiḥ.
Makṣatibhu uśravāribhu
*Svāhā*. If there is anyone who wishes to enter among bandits, they should recite this mantra over mud three times and smear it upon their body.
If they smear it upon banners, standards, pennants, drums, horns, or musical instruments, [the same protection shall apply].
One will certainly attain victory.
If one is bitten by a venomous insect,
or if afflicted by poison, or if there is a swelling on the body, [one shall be cured].
Having smeared it with enchanted mud and applied blue pigment (*añjana*) to it, one will immediately be cured.
The *Dhāraṇī-mantra of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha*: *Namo buddhāya | tathāgata mahāmaudgalyāyana svāhā | tadyathā | kiri kili | miri cili | sarvaga kiri miri | sarvaga miri | svāhā.* This *dhāraṇī*.
On the fourteenth or fifteenth day of the month, at the time when the morning star rises,
recite this eight hundred times while burning fine aloeswood incense so that the smoke does not cease.
By using eight hundred yellow flowers, one causes people to obtain blessings.
If a good man maintains this in his present life, he will remain secure and peaceful;
whatever he seeks from the depths of his heart, there shall be nothing he does not obtain.
If a woman were to transform into a man and,
with a sincere heart, practice this path and recite and uphold it for one day and one night during the six periods, she would [attain the fruit].
One shall eliminate the sins of three *kalpas* and never again enter the evil realms.
This should be practiced during the cool seasons of spring and autumn—specifically the third, fourth, eighth, and ninth months.

The *dhāraṇī* of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva: *Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*. *Tathāgata*, *kūli kūli*, *ṭhaṭha ṭhaṭha*, *vadhūs*, *mamiprala*, *haraṭa*, *svāhā*. One should recite this *dhāraṇī* three times at dawn with a sincere mind while recollecting the Buddha.
Reciting this brings all auspiciousness.

This is the *Dhāraṇī for Repentance and the Casting of Flowers*. *Namo buddhānāṃ* *Kṣaṇe kṣaṇe mahāmaudgalyāyana svāhā* *Tantrita ili cili mili tili ili mili* *Bhāṇi maṅgali svāhā* This is the supreme *dhāraṇī* held by the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Always on the fourteenth day of the month, bathe the body and perform prostrations and repentance during the three periods of the night.
At the end of the final watch, recite the text once and cast one flower;
continue this until eight hundred recitations have been completed and eight hundred flowers have been cast.

Dhāraṇī for Eliminating Calamities and Illnesses, for Extinguishing Poisons, and for Throwing Away Swellings: *tadyathā | mamamuni | mamamuni | mamapiśā | svāhā*. If there is anyone with a swelling disease...
One should empower it with this dhāraṇī-mantra.
It is also beneficial to recite the mantra over medicinal herbs one hundred and eight times and apply them.
For malignant boils and sores, recite the following dhāraṇī many times: *tatoḍe khikhile makhile mogale piśāce mahāpiśāce svāhā*. First, apply this to the sore.
Thereafter, maintain this by reciting it one hundred and eight times daily;
after seven days of such incantation, the illness will be cured.

From the *Sūryagarbha*, the *Aksyarakṣā-dhāraṇī*: *tadyathā* | *cakṣu-pa* | *śaraṇa-kṣve* | *karma-kṣve* | *anajana-nila-kṣve* | *pārthiva-gulma* | *nīvara-ṇatva* | *akṣi-sthita-ruci* | *vimati-supta-karma-supta* | *phale-supta* | *alidali-tale* | *dhanale* | *kṣetrapa-ci* | *lūraspe* | *mahālūraspe* | *rallana* | *kṣaradi* | *svāhā*. This dhāraṇī is used for the protection of the eyes.
Three times during the day and three times at night,
recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times;
by rubbing [the eyes] with the hand, eye diseases will be cured.
One should give rise to a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings,
repent of all transgressions before the Buddha,
fashion images of the Buddha, and transcribe the *Sūryagarbha*.
At that time, one should prepare an eye medicine using sea foam,
the root of licorice (yaṣṭimadhu), harītakī, āmalaka, and vibhītaka;
these should be ground together and mixed with honey.
Furthermore, take the heart of a tortoise and roast it over a fire until it is cooked and dry. Then,
combine it with the aforementioned medicine, grind them together, and thoroughly mix the compound.
Recite this dhāraṇī mantra eight thousand times and apply it to the eyelids for seven days;
one should practice mindfulness of the Buddha through these causes and conditions.
Within the cycle of birth and death until the attainment of Buddhahood,
one shall never lose one's eyesight and shall always possess pure vision.
According to the *Caturmahārājakāyika-mantra-sūtra*, the Four Heavenly Kings constantly observe the four continents.
The first is named King Vaiśravaṇa;
the second is King Dhṛtarāṣṭra;
the third is King Virūḍhaka.
Fourth is the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa, with his attendants Ucchāmañji, Palumāñji, Pātudhī, and Śaṅkhaśa.
All such matters can be accomplished.
It is said that there is a mountain named Vajra where practitioners of the Way and various devas dwell.
Various practitioners of the Way were practicing the path there;
they had attained the five supernatural powers and were able to perform transformations.
One practitioner of the Way was named Aha; he had attained the five supernatural powers and was able to perform transformations.
The Buddhas named Sudarśana, Atāyudha, Sāgara, and Vighuṣṭaśabda all thought thus and spoke these words of incantation themselves:
"I behold the birthplaces of all the Buddhas."
When the disciples of the Buddhas pass away among the people,
the lineage of the devas is thereby extinguished;
from within that state, they give rise to sorrowful reflection.
Desiring to bring about swift liberation, take refuge in the practitioner of the Way.
O Great Heavenly King who rules over the four continents,
listen to my words as I recite this incantation-sūtra.
For the sake of saving the people,
he prepared flour-mash and gruel for the spirits and deities,
and then recited the incantations.
When you let down your hair, Brahmā shall protect your head;
Śaśimi shall protect it as your overseer;
and the Moon shall protect your forehead.
The Sun shall protect your eyes;
the Stars shall protect your kidneys;
the Gandharvas shall protect your navel.
Abhini shall protect your buttocks;
itsari-kūli shall protect your lower abdomen;
and the lunar mansions (nakṣatras) shall protect your life.
Those who dwell within the four continents—
whether they be good or evil— Sūma shall protect your spleen;
the devas shall be harmonious and Ananta shall protect it.
Those ascetics and brahmins who are the Four Great Kings, lords of the four continents,
shall protect your home.
Śakata-dhvaja shall protect your knees;
Sarvabhūtabhakṣa shall protect your feet;
Mahākāla shall protect your hands.
Do not be afraid; have no fear in this, and may it bring you auspiciousness.
That Great Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa is the most honored among all ghosts, spirits, and rākṣasas.
He issued a command to all ghosts, spirits, and rākṣasas, saying:
"Recite this dhāraṇī, this great dhāraṇī; its efficacy shall be swift.
It shall cause exhaustion, confusion, and sleep."
May nothing whatsoever fail to be accomplished.
Thus it is:
Hani hani khani khani dhukhani khaji khaji khaji ji ji ti-tu-lai-ta, Great Heavenly King.
The most honored among all the gandharvas commanded all the gandharvas,
and they then recited this mantra:
Having obtained this mantra and great mantra, whatever one practices will be swiftly accomplished.
There shall be no exhaustion, distraction, or sleepiness, and nothing whatsoever shall fail to be achieved.
Hā ān hā ān hā ān | Pāṭī pāṭī pāṭī | Jīri jiri | Vīri vīti | Mandinī | Pāṭinī | Virūḍhaka, the Great Heavenly King.
He is the most honored among all kumbhāṇḍas;
he commands all kumbhāṇḍas and then utters this mantra:
Having obtained this great mantra, whatever one undertakes will be swiftly accomplished;
even if distracted or drowsy, nothing shall fail to be achieved. Thus it is said:
*Anani ahaṃdara haṃma ti-ma ti mahā-ma ti ma-te ma-te ma-ta ma-ti kṣu-jñi kṣu-jñi vi-kṣu-jñi-vi-lo-bha-cha*—the Great Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa.
The most honored among all nāgas,
he commanded the nāgas and they immediately recited this mantra;
the efficacy of this great mantra was swift.
Thus, through the dissipation of distractions and sleep, one attains the state of having nothing left unaccomplished.
*Māye māye māye māte guji viguji*. When the Heavenly King spoke this incantation-sūtra, [the world was transformed].
The earth shook everywhere;
those who disturbed the people were all struck with terror, their hair standing on end.
As for those who know this King of Mantras Sūtra:
There is no further fear or dread;
there is no suffering from headaches, nor do the eyes reel or the ears ache.
Neither the nose, lips, mouth, teeth, tongue, cheeks, chin, navel, nor the heart experiences any pain.
If there is swelling of the abdomen, swelling of the flanks, pain in the hands, pain in the navel, pain in the spleen, pain in the knees, or pain in the feet—
if all such various sufferings and pains are entirely removed,
then neither humans nor non-humans will be able to falsely harass them.
Neither the Pūtanas nor the Devas can cause harm;
neither the Nāgas nor the Gandharvas can do so either.
Whether they be garuḍas, kumbhāṇḍas,
ghosts, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas,
or the spirits who dwell by latrines.
Neither hungry ghosts, nor śeṣa-śeṣas,
nor vāyasa-rūpas, nor ātma-maras,
nor gandharvas shall be able to falsely harass them.
Furthermore, may the sun, moon, stars, planets, wind,
and cold miasmas all be eliminated; may they protect his body,
causing all malevolent influences to vanish and a hundred ailments to be healed.
Homage to all those who are auspicious, virtuous, and endowed with the excellence of diligence.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Having prostrated at their feet, he then spoke this mantra:
May my incantations be fulfilled according to my wishes.
*Dhāraṇī-saṃgraha*, Volume Ten.
